title: servicelb-controller's disable_rp_filter() EROFS-crashes inside the real DaemonSet container (containerd CRI masks /proc/sys, capabilities/AppArmor-unconfined don't unmask it)
description:
ANSWER: deploy/daemonset.yaml's servicelb-controller crashloops on startup on the k3s-on-Lima rig (beep-node-a/b) -- disable_rp_filter() (src/lib.rs, added by beep-o1b/b404db7) fails writing to /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter with EROFS, because containerd's CRI-managed OCI spec marks /proc/sys read-only for non-privileged containers by default; the daemonset's privileged:false + CAP_BPF/NET_ADMIN/PERFMON + appArmorProfile:Unconfined does NOT unmask it (capabilities/AppArmor are separate from mount-level readonlyPaths).

EVIDENCE (beep-yg7's new :sha-image-override rig, which is the first thing to ever exercise this code path through the real deploy/daemonset.yaml container -- see that PR):
  warning: setrlimit(RLIMIT_MEMLOCK) failed (harmless on memcg-accounted kernels)
  Error: disabling reverse-path filter
  Caused by:
      0: writing 0 to /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter
      1: Read-only file system (os error 30)

Reproduced 3 independent ways on beep-node-a/b (v1.36.4+k3s1, containerd v2.3.3), deterministic, regardless of which image runs the write:
  1. the real DaemonSet's own PID 1 (current HEAD's beep-controller binary)
  2. a standalone debug Pod with the SAME securityContext, PID 1 running `sh -c "echo 0 > .../rp_filter"` directly
  3. `kubectl exec` into an already-running controller pod

WHY THIS WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW: docker.io/valerauko/beep-lb:latest is built from tag v0.1.0, which is an ancestor of (predates) commit b404db7, the commit that added disable_rp_filter's self-prep -- confirmed via a merge-base ancestor check. Every existing k3s e2e rig (scripts/smoke-k3s-controller.sh, scripts/e2e-lb-k3s.sh) deploys deploy/daemonset.yaml's hardcoded :latest, so none of them have EVER run this code through the real containerd-CRI-confined DaemonSet container -- beep-o1b's "validated on a Lima rig" claim must have used a different, less-confined path (e.g. scripts/smoke.sh's bare-root-process loader, no container). beep-yg7 (this PR) makes the k3s rig deploy the commit-under-test's :sha instead of :latest, and immediately caught this real regression.

FIX OPTIONS (need an operator decision, likely another ADR alongside docs/decisions/servicelb-controller-apparmor-unconfined.md):
  (a) grant privileged: true on the container (removes ALL default readonlyPaths/maskedPaths) -- broadens the security surface beyond the existing AppArmor ADR's stated goal of avoiding exactly this;
  (b) run rp_filter disabling in a privileged initContainer instead of the main container (narrower privilege escalation, only at startup);
  (c) revisit whether hostNetwork+CAP_NET_ADMIN can be paired with a k3s/containerd config change (e.g. unmasking /proc/sys/net specifically) that's portable across the CRI implementations this project targets;
  (d) go back to option (A)/(B) from beep-o1b's original FIX OPTIONS list (host-level DaemonSet initContainer, or giving geneve0 a real address) instead of a raw filesystem write from the main container.

DONE-WHEN: deploy/daemonset.yaml's controller reaches Running with 0 crash-loop restarts on scripts/smoke-k3s-controller.sh's Lima rig, deploying the actual commit-under-test (not :latest).
close_reason: Fixed in PR https://github.com/litehop/beep/pull/109: rp_filter node-prep moved into a privileged initContainer (beep-controller --node-prep), main container stays non-privileged. scripts/smoke-k3s-controller.sh on beep-node-a/b: CONTROLLER-DEPLOY PASS (Running on both nodes, 0 restarts after 10s settle), full round-trip + FLOW_TABLE PASS. Clean-slate check on beep-node-a (geneve0 deleted, rp_filter.all=2 beforehand) confirmed --node-prep creates geneve0 then sets rp_filter=0 on all+geneve0 independent of the rig's own pre-existing workaround.

title: shipped DaemonSet/README omit rp_filter=0 for address-less geneve0 -- decapped LB packets silently dropped on a real cluster
description:
ROOT CAUSE of the u7s integration wall (beep-a5k / PR #74 findings, grep-verified). The kernel reverse-path filter silently drops decapped forward packets: an address-less geneve0 never gets rp_filter loose-mode (2) exception, so ip_route_input_noref returns -EXDEV and the packet dies before the backend pod's cni0/veth. Symptom: Geneve encap fires + arrives + decaps correctly (client IP + VIP intact), FLOW_TABLE gets the reverse-flow entry, but the backend pod sees ZERO packets; same-node curl to the pod IP works.

Every beep smoke/e2e script applies net.ipv4.conf.{all,geneve0}.rp_filter=0 as the required workaround (scripts/smoke-k3s-controller.sh, scripts/e2e-lb-k3s.sh, scripts/smoke-remote.sh) -- but deploy/daemonset.yaml and deploy/README.md OMIT it (grep-confirmed absent from deploy/). So beep passes its own rigs yet silently fails on any real deploy. u7s's mayor-re973 round 5 MEASURED rp_filter=2 and dismissed it as benign -- exactly the broken condition beep's own code documents.

FIX OPTIONS (operator design decision -- B vs C is a security tradeoff): (A) DaemonSet privileged initContainer runs sysctl -w on the host netns; (B) PREFERRED if viable -- the loader (already creates/owns geneve0, holds CAP_NET_ADMIN) gives geneve0 an address/route so it earns rp_filter's loose-mode exception WITHOUT weakening anti-spoof globally; (C) loader sets rp_filter=0 itself at attach (self-contained but weakens anti-spoof on 'all'). Document in deploy/README.md regardless. B's feasibility needs a quick check (external-mode geneve0 is address-less by design -- does assigning an address conflict with the dataplane?).

DONE-WHEN: the SHIPPED deploy artifact delivers LB traffic on a default-rp_filter kernel with NO manual sysctl, validated on a Lima rig. Dataplane bead -> host gate + scripts/smoke.sh (or fold into beep-my4). NOT the same as beep-1d4 (pod-CIDR observability) nor beep-my4 (live confirm) -- this is the production fix. Cross-ref beep-a5k, beep-my4.
notes: Filed follow-on beep-bwh: no outer-Geneve-source validation exists today (checked ebpf/src/main.rs's geneve_ingress -- only tkey.tunnel_id is checked, remote_ipv4 is trusted, no peer-node allowlist). This PR ships rp_filter=0 per the operator decision; beep-bwh tracks the compensating control.
close_reason: PR #75 opened: https://github.com/litehop/beep/pull/75 -- controller self-preps geneve0 + rp_filter=0 at startup; deploy/README.md documents the deliberate revisit-if-new-risks decision; docs corrected; follow-on beep-bwh filed for outer-Geneve-source validation (checked, not built).

title: fix(servicelb): pin the eBPF maps so a loader restart keeps flow state
description:
Route every map through EbpfLoader::map_pin_path so a loader restart reuses the
pinned maps instead of creating empty ones.

Today only links and programs are pinned, at src/main.rs:336 and :363.
Ebpf::load creates a fresh, empty map set on every start, and attach_and_pin
then calls bpf_link_update to swap the new program onto the existing pinned
link. The dataplane keeps forwarding, but against empty conntrack tables, so
every established flow breaks. In a DaemonSet that happens on every image
rollout, eviction, and OOM kill.

ai/extended-context/ebpf-lb-dataplane.md line 133 already promises the
opposite: pinned under /sys/fs/bpf so restarts keep flow state.

Secondary win: during the swap the old and new map sets coexist, so peak
kernel memory is roughly double the steady-state 1.82 MiB. Reuse removes that
spike.

aya 0.14 supports this directly. EbpfLoader::map_pin_path routes each map
through MapData::create_pinned_by_name, which tries bpf_get_object on the pin
path first and only creates a map when the pin is absent.

DONE WHEN: a loader restart preserves conntrack entries, proved by a smoke
test that holds a connection open across a restart and fails if the entries
are lost.
notes: INVARIANT for Phase 5, from the 2026-09-05 review discussion: reconciliation (a Service/EndpointSlice change) is a live per-key write to VIP_MAP and POD_TARGETS via bpf_map_update_elem/delete_elem, per ai/extended-context/ebpf-lb-dataplane.md:132 (load programs once, write maps on change, idle). It is NOT a program reload and NOT a process restart, so it never by itself resets the FWD_FLOW/REV_FLOW LRU conntrack maps -- those are separate kernel map objects untouched by a config-map write. The only things that reset the LRU maps are reload or restart with fresh unpinned maps, which is exactly the hazard this bead fixes. A well-built Phase 5 controller must never reload on a config change. Corollary: do NOT wire map auto-resize into the reconcile loop, since resize needs create-new-and-swap, which WOULD reset conntrack unless migrated.
close_reason: PR #1585 opened: pin eBPF maps via EbpfLoader::map_pin_path so loader restart reuses pinned maps and preserves FWD_FLOW/REV_FLOW conntrack; restart-preservation smoke test added and verified to fail on revert.

title: fix(servicelb): drop rather than forward a REV_FLOW miss on uplink egress
description:
Change the uplink-egress reverse-flow miss path from TC_ACT_OK to a drop plus
a counter, once the packet has been positively identified as backend traffic.

uplink_egress_return at servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:533 maps a failed REV_FLOW
lookup to TC_ACT_OK. On an LRU eviction the backend Pod's raw reply then
leaves the node unencapsulated, carrying a pod-CIDR source address onto the
underlay. That both stalls the connection and leaks a pod-source packet,
which is worse than dropping it.

The forward decap path already treats its equivalent miss as fatal:
geneve_ingress maps a failed try_geneve_decap_return to TC_ACT_SHOT. The
egress path should be consistent.

Care needed: try_uplink_egress_return returns None both for "not our traffic"
and for "reverse entry missing", and today both collapse to TC_ACT_OK.
Non-ServiceLB traffic must still pass untouched, so the two cases have to be
separated before a drop is safe. The POD_TARGETS membership gate bead
provides exactly that positive identification cheaply.

DONE WHEN: an evicted reverse entry produces a drop and an incremented
counter, with a regression test that fails if the fallback returns to
TC_ACT_OK for identified backend traffic, and unrelated egress traffic still
passes.
close_reason: PR #1624 opened

title: design(servicelb): flow-table admission control
description:
Decide how this dataplane admits a flow into the conntrack table before
anyone picks a max_entries ceiling, because table size cannot fix a table
that 8192 packets can cycle.

uplink_ingress inserts into FWD_FLOW at servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:238
immediately after the VIP_MAP match, with no TCP state check, no SYN gate,
and no validation of any kind. Any packet that reaches a service address
creates an entry, so an off-path sender can evict all legitimate flow state
with 8192 packets from varying source ports, which is milliseconds of
traffic. Sizing against expected legitimate concurrency does not help.

LRU never rejects, it evicts, so the failure is silent rather than loud.
Forward evictions drop return traffic; reverse evictions leak an
unencapsulated reply. Both are covered by sibling beads.

Research and decide among:

- Promote on evidence of bidirectionality. New flows enter a small
  unconfirmed pool and move to the main table only when the return direction
  is observed. Modelled on nf_conntrack's unreplied versus assured states.
  Protocol-agnostic, so one mechanism covers TCP, UDP, and QUIC. This is the
  recommended starting point if only one thing gets built.
- QUIC specifics. RFC 9000 section 8.1.2's Retry token is a first-class
  address-validation handshake. Better still, this dataplane already mints
  the DCID, so minting it with an embedded MAC makes every later short-header
  packet self-authenticating and prevents state creation outright. Note that
  draft-ietf-quic-load-balancers was declined at doc line 108 on routing
  grounds; the anti-flush property is a separate argument that was not
  weighed. RFC 9000 section 14.1's 1200-byte Initial minimum also raises
  flood cost roughly thirtyfold over a bare TCP SYN.
- TCP. A SYN gate is cheap but weak, since setting the bit is free. SYN
  cookies are the real analogue and need care in a load balancer that does
  not terminate TCP.
- UDP. No L4 signal exists at all: no flag, no handshake, no field
  distinguishing a first packet from a mid-stream one. The available levers
  are per-source-prefix rate limiting on state creation and per-service
  opt-in.

DONE WHEN: a written decision on the admission mechanism exists, and the
max_entries ceiling is settled as a consequence of it rather than guessed
independently.
notes:
DECLINED, with rationale, from the 2026-09-05 review discussion: runtime dynamic resize of the conntrack maps (scale max_entries up/down within a min/max range based on live traffic). Two independent reasons. (1) Economics: the table is ~120 bytes/entry (measured), so shrinking a tiny-cluster table from 8192 to 1024 entries saves ~860 KiB -- under 0.1% of a 1 GB node -- while the scale-DOWN direction a tiny cluster wants is the hardest to measure (silent LRU eviction, no live count). (2) Timing: a control loop reacts in seconds; a sudden burst (HN front page) saturates in milliseconds, so you cannot autoscale out of a burst -- by the time you detect+allocate+migrate+swap it has passed or already thrashed. Burst survival comes from graceful LRU degradation (never returns E2BIG, evicts LRU, self-heals on next packet, fixed footprint regardless of load -- cannot OOM from traffic) plus a pre-provisioned fixed ceiling plus admission control (this bead) to protect established flows from a flood of new ones. The legitimate-traffic burst and the malicious flush attack are the SAME mechanism seen from two sides. Right-sizing belongs at load time (discrete tiny/default/large profiles from node facts), informed by observability metrics (mayor-aie31.22), not a runtime swap. Corollary already on aie31.8: do not wire resize into the reconcile loop.
Findings doc: ai/findings/2026-09-06-mayor-aie31.11-flow-table-admission-control.md (branch worker/agent-aea30cb1ec81c8e99, commit 6a6cdbba). Recommendation: adopt option (a) promote-on-bidirectionality (nf_conntrack unreplied/assured, observable at ingress because symmetric return puts both legs on one node) as the mandatory protocol-agnostic foundation; ceiling derived as a consequence -> split FWD_FLOW into FWD_PENDING=2048 (only flood-exposed tier) + FWD_MAIN=8192 (unchanged but now justified). QUIC self-authenticating minted-DCID MAC (option b) conditional on g3lag choosing CID-based keying; reject TCP SYN-cookies (needs TCP termination). Couplings flagged: g3lag (anti-flush is a new argument for CID keying), aie31.21 (FWD_FLOW becomes affinity store; two maps must be designed jointly), aie31.20/aie31.17 (map substrate). Awaiting operator decision.
## critical-reviewer findings — findings-doc — mayor-aie31.11

**Verdict**: LGTM-with-suggestions

**Confirmed findings** (must be true, evidence cited):
- [MED] The core topology claim is TRUE: forward (`uplink_ingress`) and return (`geneve_ingress` VNI_RET) legs run on the same ingress node by construction, so the return-path `FWD_FLOW.get` at main.rs:514 genuinely is a bidirectionality proof. Evidence: `main.rs:246` inserts keyed on ingress-local tuple, `main.rs:431` (`RevFlowValue.ingress_node_ip = tkey.remote_ipv4`) captures the originating node, `main.rs:598` (`uplink_egress_return`) Geneve-redirects the reply back to that exact node. No fix needed — this confirms the doc's foundation is sound.
- [MED] The DONE-WHEN ceiling table splits `FWD_PENDING`/`FWD_MAIN` for TCP/UDP but defines no PENDING tier for the QUIC CID map, leaving the Answer's "closes...for TCP, UDP, and QUIC with one mechanism" claim structurally unbacked for QUIC. Evidence: doc lines 197-201 (table has only "Main (QUIC)", no "Pending (QUIC)") vs. line 14 and line 122 ("QUIC? Same — the first server response promotes the flow"). Suggested fix: add a QUIC PENDING/MAIN split to the ceiling table or explicitly justify why QUIC's CID map doesn't need one.
- [MED] Option (b)'s "LB mints DCID with embedded MAC" mechanism rests on the same "LB-minted CID" model that sibling finding mayor-g3lag (committed 12s earlier, same session, commit 78c738bf) explicitly refutes as unrealizable for a non-terminating dataplane under BOTH of g3lag's realizable keying paths — pass-through has no CID map, and QUIC-LB method 3 has the *backend* mint the CID, not the LB. Evidence: aie31.11 doc lines 152-161 ("this dataplane already mints the DCID... If it mints it with an embedded keyed MAC") vs. g3lag doc lines 222-225 ("the anti-forgery property comes from the backend's encrypted server_id encoding, not an LB-minted MAC... not off a MAC the LB stamped"). aie31.11's framing ("if and only if mayor-g3lag chooses CID-based keying") implies (b) becomes buildable as-written once g3lag picks CID keying; per g3lag it does not — it needs redesign to validate a backend-minted value, not describe minting one. Suggested fix: reframe (b) as "validate backend-minted QUIC-LB server_id" conditional on g3lag's method 3, not "LB mints DCID+MAC" conditional on "CID-based keying."

**Suspicions** (worth the maintainer's attention, but I did not confirm):
- The non-atomic PENDING get→insert→delete promotion sequence is claimed benign under all interleavings. Why suspicious: claim is asserted, not demonstrated against concurrent-CPU BPF map semantics. To verify: trace a concrete two-CPU interleaving (forward re-insert racing a return-triggered promote/remove) against BPF map atomicity guarantees, or defer to implementation-time review.

**Not reviewed** (out of scope for this deliverable's checklist):
- netfilter `early_drop`/`IPS_ASSURED` internals — doc itself discloses these are from established knowledge, not a fetched source.
- RFC 9000 §8.1.2/§14.1 text — not independently re-fetched; relied on general knowledge and g3lag's own overlapping RFC citations.

**Meta**: reviewed at 2026-09-06T09:44:31Z, deliverable size (1 file / 285 lines), checklist items checked (5/5 findings-doc checklist items: citation quality, verdict soundness, follow-on beads, uncertainty language, file location).

Overall: the mandatory recommendation (adopt promote-on-bidirectionality as the protocol-agnostic foundation) is sound, its topology premise is verified true against `main.rs`, and the fallback for QUIC under 4-tuple pass-through (option (a) + §14.1 size gate, no MAC) is real and matches g3lag's own conclusion — the operator can rely on that core recommendation. The two MED findings above affect only the DONE-WHEN table's QUIC completeness and the conditional/optional MAC layer, not the mandatory foundation.
DECISION (operator 2026-09-07): ACCEPT option (a) promote-on-bidirectionality as the flow-table admission foundation -- 2-tier, new flows enter FWD_PENDING and promote to FWD_MAIN only when the return leg is observed (protects established flows from a spoofed flood). Protocol-agnostic; QUIC uses the same (a) since g3lag chose tuple-based, so option-b DCID-MAC is NOT built for the MVP. CONSTRAINT (operator): the map sizes (FWD_PENDING, FWD_MAIN, and any per-protocol tier) MUST be CONFIGURABLE by the userspace DaemonSet at load time -- NOT hard-coded consts in the eBPF object. Implementation pending under the aie31 build phases; bead stays open as impl-ready.
close_reason: Implemented and PR opened: two-tier promote-on-bidirectionality flow admission (FWD_PENDING/FWD_MAIN split), configurable map sizes, VipBackend value type for aie31.21 forward-compat. PR https://github.com/litehop/u7s/pull/1611

title: fix(servicelb): POD_TARGETS holds one port per pod, breaking multi-port Services
description:
POD_TARGETS maps a pod IP to a single u16, so any Pod with two distinct
target ports is already mis-DNATed in shipped code.

servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:130 declares HashMap<u32, u16> keyed on pod IP
alone, with no port set and no protocol dimension. The forward decap reads it
at line 345 to pick the DNAT target port. One value per pod cannot represent:

- a multi-port Service, for example 80 to 8080 alongside 443 to 8443
- a Pod backing two Services, for example app traffic plus a metrics endpoint
- TCP and UDP on different ports

HTTP/3 happens to survive this. A Service declares TCP 443 and UDP 443 as two
port entries, because a Service port entry carries exactly one protocol, and
both point at the same target port. The map stores only the number, so one
entry serves both. That is coincidence, not coverage.

Wire-format wrinkle: widening the map is not sufficient on its own. The
forward Geneve option carries only the raw pod IP, per the settled decision
at ai/extended-context/ebpf-lb-dataplane.md line 149, so the backend cannot
disambiguate two target ports for one pod. Either the option grows, or the
backend re-keys off what the packet still carries at decap time, namely the
VIP, the VIP port, and the protocol. That information is present and
sufficient, so the fix exists, but it is a design change rather than a
widening of the value type.

Blocks Phase 5, mayor-9gr0n, for a plain multi-port Service.

DONE WHEN: a Service with two target ports on one Pod routes both correctly,
covered by a test that fails against the current single-value map.
close_reason: PR #1573 opened

title: servicelb-ebpf: try_geneve_decap_return carries over all-zero L2 header from L3 underlay onto client-bound redirect -> PACKET_OTHERHOST drop on a real Ethernet client-ingress
description: Found by beep-4ni's genuine cross-node smoke (PR #119, cf21aca). On the return leg, try_geneve_decap_return's final client-bound redirect blindly carries over the all-zero synthetic L2 header that a peer's L3-only uplink (wg0) leaves on the packet. Redirecting that into a REAL Ethernet egress device gets it eth_type_trans-classified PACKET_OTHERHOST and dropped. NOT IPv6-specific -- affects v4 AND v6. Bites a real production topology: Ethernet client-ingress + WireGuard(L3) backend-uplink. The #119 smoke works around it TEST-SIDE ONLY (node-a client uplink is an ipip/ip6tnl tunnel dev, ARPHRD_TUNNEL, no MAC check) -- the underlying dataplane bug remains. Real fix (eBPF): synthesize a valid L2 header for the client-bound redirect when the egress device is Ethernet, rather than carrying over the L3-underlay's all-zero header. v1 production-readiness relevant; candidate 0.3.0 gate (operator to decide). Cross-ref PR #119 Risk section.
notes: PR #121 opened: https://github.com/litehop/beep/pull/121. Fix: try_geneve_decap_return's redirect_client_bound now branches on UPLINK_CONFIG.l2_hlen == ETH_HLEN, calling bpf_redirect_neigh for a real Ethernet client egress (resolves L2 via FIB+neighbor lookup) instead of carrying over geneve0's all-zero L2 header; tunnel egress unchanged (plain bpf_redirect). New regression rig scripts/smoke-wg-2node-ethclient.sh (real veth uplink, not ipip/ip6tnl) demonstrated FAIL-before (curl timeout, PACKET_OTHERHOST-consistent silent drop) / PASS-after. scripts/smoke-wg-2node-dualstack.sh's existing tunnel-egress round trip confirmed unaffected (v4+v6). Full 5-command host gate green (clippy/build verified on genuine Linux via beep-node-a, not just macOS). Left in_progress per dispatch -- mayor closes on merge.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #121 (merged 02:27Z, commit on main). Return-leg client-bound redirect now synthesizes a valid L2 header on Ethernet egress via bpf_redirect_neigh (NULL params → kernel FIB+neigh resolution), gated on the existing UPLINK_CONFIG.l2_hlen==ETH_HLEN; tunnel egress unchanged. No common/ map-layout or loader-CLI change. Verified fail-before/pass-after on new rig scripts/smoke-wg-2node-ethclient.sh, dualstack rig unregressed; Sonnet review LGTM #5262625278. Follow-on hardening: beep-puf (cold-neighbor-cache variant).

title: test-fidelity: bare-loader 2-node WG rig is a same-node self-loop (NODE_ALLOW peer attestation); genuine node-a->node-b data traversal needs the controller or real hardware
description: Found during beep-7qm.7 (PR #119, Risk section). beep_common::peer_node_admission (landed ec07447, AFTER beep-n24's fix) makes a BARE loader (no controller / no Node-watch) admit a Geneve decap ONLY when the outer source == the decapsulating node's own --node-ip, with no CLI knob to whitelist a different peer. Consequence: every bare-loader beep-node-a/beep-node-b round trip -- beep-7qm.7's dual-stack one AND the pre-existing v4 smoke-wg-2node -- is structurally a same-node self-loop on the BACKEND node (node-b is both ingress-for-admission and backend; its --uplink-iface catches the client veth packet). wg0 genuinely carries the WireGuard handshake + has the loader attached on node-a, but client DATA packets never physically cross wg0. So the 2-node rig proves decap/DNAT/re-encap/return on a node (real value) but NOT genuine cross-node data-plane traversal. To get real traversal: run the controller (Node-watch populates NODE_ALLOW with peer node IPs) in the rig, OR validate on real hardware (beep-903 phase). ALSO correct ai/prompts/mayor-dispatch-template.md's stale 'Known blocker' section: it still cites beep-n24's co-located martian-drop; beep-n24 is CLOSED (fixed by #93, which added the beep-client VM), and this NODE_ALLOW self-loop is the current real constraint. Relevant to v1 cross-node production-readiness claims.
notes: PR #119 (same-node dual-stack smoke) reviewed LGTM-with-suggestions (2026-09-19). HELD as DRAFT pending operator disposition: the 'cross-node' label is misleading (self-loop). Plan under discussion: upgrade #119 into a GENUINE cross-node test = (1) seed node-B NODE_ALLOW with node-A's underlay IP as a fixture (mimic controller Node-watch; mechanism TBD: loader flag vs bpftool-write the pinned map), (2) originate client on node-A so traffic encaps + crosses wg0 to node-B, (3) assert backend observes REAL client IP for v4 AND v6. Also fix reviewer's LOW nit: dump_evidence's client-veth/netns block (smoke-wg-2node-remote.sh:323-328) runs unconditionally -> noise in smoke-wg-2node.sh's v4 failure dump; gate it behind CLIENT_NETNS being set. beep-4ni gates 0.3.0 (operator direction, being confirmed).
close_reason: PR #119 upgraded to a genuine cross-node round trip (both v4+v6 PASS, wg0-traversal evidenced, client-IP preservation asserted) via bidirectional NODE_ALLOW bpftool seeding (no dataplane change) + ipip/ip6tnl client uplink (sidesteps a newly-found try_geneve_decap_return L2 gap). Template correction done. New HEAD cf21aca, PR left draft for mayor re-ready.

title: controller: widen POD_TARGETS pinned-map key to 16 bytes (matches beep-7qm.4/.5 layout; unblocks #118 memory-smoke)
description: PR #118 widened POD_TARGETS key to [u8;16] in loader+ebpf+common, but the controller/ crate is a THIRD consumer that opens the same pinned map with a 4-byte key. memory-smoke fails: 'map POD_TARGETS is not a BPF_MAP_TYPE_HASH / invalid key size 4, expected 16' -- beep-controller cannot open the pinned maps and fails to attach. Fix: widen the controller-side POD_TARGETS key to the 16-byte shape, ideally by importing the shared beep-common key type (per the byte-identical-map-layout convention -- the controller must not skew independently). Likely site: controller/src/apply.rs PinnedMaps open pattern. Lands ON #118's branch worker/agent-af07250ba966ff9ab so memory-smoke re-runs green.

title: epic: endpoint-churn resilience -- selective conntrack eviction on endpoint removal (v1 requirement)
description: Operator (2026-09-19, FIRM): a real production cluster continuously sees endpoint add/remove, so v1 production-ready code MUST accommodate selective conntrack eviction on endpoint removal. The DESIGN is already DECIDED in mayor-aie31.21 (eviction table settled: UDP FWD_FLOW delete mandatory; TCP FWD_FLOW delete YES; REV_FLOW delete both protocols for pod-IP-reuse safety) but is NOT YET IMPLEMENTED anywhere in the repo (confirmed by the beep-5lw multi-pod plan audit -- pin implemented, eviction absent). This epic tracks IMPLEMENTING that decided design. Multi-pod backend LB (beep-5lw) DEPENDS on this: N endpoints means churn, which orphans flows pinned to departed pods unless eviction exists. Future-session epic. Part of the v1.0 functional-correctness gate (beep-xfa), BEFORE audits/docs.

title: audit(ipv6): phased dual-stack implementation plan + decomposition for beep-7qm
description: beep-7qm.1 confirmed the Lima rig is IPv6-capable (ULA-static) and beep's own code is IPv4-only. Produce the phased dual-stack IMPLEMENTATION plan and decompose beep-7qm into implementable sub-beads. Read the v4-only surfaces end-to-end: src/main.rs + src/lib.rs (node_ip/pod_cidr/VIP typed Ipv4Addr/Ipv4Cidr), the NODE_ALLOW / bpf_tunnel_key.remote_ipv4 gate and VIP/backend/conntrack map key layouts in common/src/lib.rs + ebpf/src/main.rs (dual-stack vs v6-only; inner vs outer Geneve header; map key size for a 128-bit addr), and smoke.sh/smoke-remote.sh + smoke-wg-2node-remote.sh v4 literals. Confirm the planned v6 SMOKE approach works on beep-node-a using beep-7qm.1's proven static-ULA veth method. Findings doc + phased plan; file sub-beads under beep-7qm (one at a time, appending each ID to this bead's notes).
acceptance_criteria: Findings doc records a phased dual-stack plan (what changes in common/src, ebpf, smoke rig; dual-stack vs v6-only decision points for the operator; map-layout impact), a confirmed v6-testable-on-lima approach, and a set of implementable sub-beads filed under beep-7qm.
notes:
DESCOPED/STOPPED 2026-09-19: over-scoped vs operator intent -- they wanted a plain nc/ping6 confirmation that Lima IPv6 connectivity actually works, NOT a full dual-stack implementation plan from step 1. Lightweight verification done directly by the mayor. The dual-stack implementation PLAN remains a valid FUTURE step for beep-7qm but is DEFERRED until beep-7qm implementation is prioritized (and until multi-uplink beep-eix.3-.6 lands, so any plan reflects the new per-uplink Config shape).
RE-ACTIVATED 2026-09-19: NOT deferred. Operator clarified IPv6 is real v1 work + it is a FIRM architectural constraint (beep must run on IPv6-only nodes, no NAT64/DNS64). The earlier 'descoped' note applies ONLY to the mayor having over-scoped this BEFORE the requested plain-nc feasibility check; that check is now DONE and CONFIRMED (precise layered picture: memory lima-ipv6-reconciled-with-u7s -- static-ULA veth + WireGuard testable, plain Lima network v6 absent). This decomposition/plan is the immediate NEXT workstream, sequenced to start right after multi-uplink (beep-eix.3-.6) merges so it plans against the SETTLED per-uplink Config rather than code mid-change. Sequencing to avoid rework, NOT deferral.
OPERATOR STEER (2026-09-19): (1) sequencing IPv6 after multi-uplink is FINE. (2) Testing v6 over WireGuard (cross-node, wg0) is an accepted GOOD FIRST STEP -- make it the first testable slice of the decomposition (aligns with memory lima-ipv6-reconciled-with-u7s: WG is where cross-node v6 is Lima-testable; the plain eth0/user-v2 net is NOT). (3) IPv6 goes LOCK-STEP with multi-interface: build dual-stack ON the per-uplink Config that beep-eix.3-.6 establishes; the wg0 uplink is the natural v6 entry point (KIND rides the same per-uplink COUNT structures -- address-family-aware per-uplink admission/redirect + v6-capable FLOW_TABLE/NODE_ALLOW keys). The decomposition MUST start from the MERGED multi-uplink Config, not today's -- another reason to sequence right after beep-eix.3-.6 lands.
Filed sub-bead 1/5 (first, per operator steer): beep-7qm.3 -- v6-over-WireGuard cross-node round-trip test (beep-node-a/-b).
Filed sub-bead 2/5: beep-7qm.4 -- widen LbFrontKey/LbFrontBackend/RevFlowValue/NODE_ALLOW to the ipv4_mapped_v6 128-bit shape (Phase A+B).
Filed sub-bead 3/5: beep-7qm.5 -- dual-stack inner-packet parsing + Geneve tunnel-key family branch (rest of Phase B).
Filed sub-bead 4/5: beep-7qm.6 -- widen loader CLI/types (Fixture/Ipv4Cidr/node_ip) off Ipv4Addr onto IpAddr (Phase C).
Filed sub-bead 5/5 (final, dataplane-complete): beep-7qm.7 -- dual-stack VIP round trip smoke test (v4 client + v6 client to the same Service), which is beep-7qm's own top-level acceptance criterion for the dual-stack half. Decomposition complete: beep-7qm.3 (WG v6 plumbing, first) -> .4 (common+ebpf key widening) -> .5 (ebpf family branching) -> .6 (loader CLI/types) -> .7 (dual-stack smoke).

Dual-stack vs v6-only surfaced as two independent forks (front/backend family, underlay/peer family) for the operator, not decided here. 5 sub-beads filed under beep-7qm: beep-7qm.3 (v6-over-WireGuard cross-node round-trip test, first per operator steer, no dataplane code) -> beep-7qm.4 (beep-common+ebpf key widening) -> beep-7qm.5 (ebpf family branching) -> beep-7qm.6 (loader CLI/types) -> beep-7qm.7 (dual-stack smoke, beep-7qm's own top-level acceptance criterion). description: De-risk the ratified multi-symmetric-uplink design (beep-eix) before implementation. **Findings**: All three conclusions verified sound.

Q2 (ingress-ifindex keyed lookup): Verifier acceptance claim is correct—reading  context field (not packet data via load_direct) and using it as HashMap key then bpf_redirect target is valid eBPF, orthogonal to the compile-time-offset constraint.

title: net/servicelb: IPv6 support -- dual-stack and IPv6-only fronts/underlay
description: beep needs IPv6 support in two modes -- dual-stack (v4+v6 fronts and backends served at once) and IPv6-only -- and neither exists today; no bead tracked this gap until now. The dataplane is only half-ready: the conntrack key is documented as IPv6-primary/37 bytes (docs/design/ebpf-lb-dataplane.md:96), but the live path assumes IPv4 fronts (common/src/lib.rs:532-536 states the front is always IPv4 at the wire level and vip_ip is a bare u32). The wire key was sized for v6 while the front path, backend source-port remap, Geneve remote addressing, and controller map-population are all v4-only. Scope: make front (VIP:port), pod/backend IP, and Geneve underlay endpoints IP-version-agnostic across LbFrontKey/LbFrontBackend, the conntrack key encode/decode, resolve_backend_src_port (hardcodes u32 IPv4 fronts today), Geneve encap/decap, and the userspace controller programming address families from Service.spec.ipFamilies. Related: beep-903 already carries the IPv6-only real-fleet round-trip SIGN-OFF (Tier-3) -- this bead is the implementation that gate exercises. mayor-xjy5o (QUIC CID keying) is independent. Not in v1.0 scope (beep-xfa). Likely splits during design into: key/map + controller-family plumbing, dual-stack impl, IPv6-only impl.
design: v4/v6 tension to resolve: docs/design/ebpf-lb-dataplane.md:96 (key sized IPv6-primary, 37 bytes) vs common/src/lib.rs:532-536 (front assumed IPv4, vip_ip a bare u32). First design step is the on-wire key shape for mixed families (single widened key vs per-family maps), since LbFrontKey and the conntrack-key layout MUST stay byte-identical across the kernel/user boundary (beep-common invariant).
acceptance_criteria: Dual-stack: a v4 client and a v6 client to the same type=LoadBalancer Service both round-trip end-to-end cross-node (forward + symmetric return). IPv6-only: full forward + symmetric-return round-trip works on an IPv6-only front and underlay, validated cross-node on real fleet (feeds beep-903 Tier-3). No IPv4-only regression: existing v4 smoke/e2e stays green.
notes:
v1 BLOCKER (operator 2026-09-19): dual-stack / IPv6 is a REQUIRED v1.0 (production-ready) item, alongside multi-interface (beep-eix) and the real-hardware deploy story. Bumped P3->P2, reparented under epic beep-xfa. Covers dual-stack AND IPv6-only fronts/underlay. Not near-term (north-star epic child); prioritize when v1.0 work activates.
IPv6 RIG FEASIBILITY (from beep-7qm.1 spike, 2026-09-19): the existing Lima rig CAN test IPv6/dual-stack -- NO new infra needed. CAVEAT: Lima's user-v2 usermode net gives LINK-LOCAL v6 only (no RA/DHCPv6/global routable), so tests must use STATICALLY-assigned ULA addrs on a veth fixture (guest kernel has CONFIG_IPV6=y + v6 tunnel modules; veth+ULA+ping6+ND all verified working on beep-node-a). The REAL work is beep's OWN code, not the rig: (1) node_ip/pod_cidr/VIP are Ipv4Addr/Ipv4Cidr and NODE_ALLOW is keyed on bpf_tunnel_key.remote_ipv4 -- need Ipv6/dual-stack types first; (2) smoke.sh/smoke-remote.sh hardcode v4 literals; (3) a 2-node v6 rig needs smoke-wg-2node-remote.sh setup_wg widened in 3 spots (eth0_ip 'ip -4', /24->/64, /32->/128) -- WireGuard itself is protocol-agnostic and the existing beep-node-a/-b/-client rig suffices. No follow-on infra bead needed (per the spike's own criterion).
DUAL-STACK RATIFIED (operator 2026-09-19): implement IPv6 as DUAL-STACK on BOTH axes -- (1) front/backend: a single 128-bit ipv4-mapped-v6 UNION key (LbFrontKey/LbFrontBackend/RevFlowValue + ebpf NODE_ALLOW) serving v4 AND v6 fronts; (2) underlay/peer: dual-stack Geneve tunnel + NODE_ALLOW tolerating a mixed v4/v6 node fleet. NOT v6-only (which would drop v4 fronts, violating this bead's own acceptance). v6-only NODES use the v6 side, satisfying the firm IPv6-only-node constraint. Governs beep-7qm.4/.5/.6/.7; the .4 PR body must record this decision.

title: fail loud on pod-CIDR misconfiguration: detect observed pod IPs outside configured --pod-cidr (silent mis-encap today)
description:
CORRECTED PREMISE (2026-09-16): the pod-CIDR admission check DOES exist -- controller/src/reconcile.rs:207 admits an endpoint only if node.pod_cidr.contains(pod_ip) OR pod_ip==node_ip (hostNetwork); anything else is REJECTED as anti-spoof (reconcile.rs:78-82). The DEFECT is that the rejection is SILENT. reconcile_service() is a pure function that filters rejected endpoints out of the desired set; the consumer apply_reconcile (controller/src/main.rs:119) only logs on an apply ERROR (eprintln 'controller: applying reconciled maps failed'), never on a rejected endpoint.

FAILURE MODE (Rule-12 fail-loud violation): run beep with --pod-cidr=10.42.0.0/16 (k3s default, hardcoded deploy/daemonset.yaml:84) against a cluster whose pods are on 10.244.0.0/16 (u7s). EVERY normal endpoint is rejected by the admission gate -> the VIP gets zero admitted POD_TARGETS -> dataplane has no backend to deliver to -> traffic is not delivered, with NO log identifying the cause. This is the silent baffling failure the u7s-side mayor hit for sessions (see beep-a5k).

WHAT SHOULD CHANGE: emit a loud WARN per rejected endpoint (or aggregate: 'N endpoints for svc X rejected: pod_ip outside configured pod_cidr Y') at the reconcile CALL SITE (controller/src/main.rs apply_reconcile has NodeContext + reconcile output). Keep reconcile side-effect-free: surface rejected endpoints in reconcile_service()'s RETURN so the caller logs them. Consider an additional first-watch sanity warning if the first observed EndpointSlice's pod IPs are ALL outside --pod-cidr. Raise doc prominence of --pod-cidr=<your cluster pod-CIDR> (deploy/README.md + daemonset.yaml:84 comment currently reads 'k3s default', not 'MUST match your cluster').

DESIGN CHOICE for operator: warn-only (recommended -- the anti-spoof rejection itself is correct; the gap is purely observability) vs also a controller status/metric.

DONE-WHEN: a pod-CIDR mismatch produces an explicit WARN naming the offending pod_ip + configured pod_cidr; regression test that a reconcile with an out-of-CIDR endpoint surfaces it as rejected-with-reason (test fails if the rejection goes back to silent). NOT TO TOUCH: the reconcile.rs:207 admission logic is CORRECT (anti-spoof) -- this bead adds observability around it, not a behavior change.
notes: Refined (beep-a5k round 2): this is a DAY-ONE blocker for the unmodified manifest (--pod-cidr=10.42 default vs a real cluster's CIDR), not lower-urgency -- but a DISTINCT gate from rp_filter (beep-o1b). Signature: admission-gate rejection empties POD_TARGETS and SHOTs the packet BEFORE the FLOW_TABLE insert (ebpf/src/main.rs:634 vs :790) -> FLOW_TABLE stays 0. rp_filter drop leaves FLOW_TABLE POPULATED but pod silent. u7s round-4/5 showed FLOW_TABLE populated => that failure was rp_filter (beep-o1b), NOT this gate (round-5 had already corrected --pod-cidr). Both are real day-one gates; fix both for a working shipped manifest.

title: feat/test: live-confirm beep LB delivery under u7s v0.3.0-snapshot.1 on beep-smoke
description: Phase-2 follow-on to beep-a5k's diagnosis (ai/findings/2026-09-16-beep-a5k-u7s-integration-diagnosis.md). Live-confirm on beep-smoke (single-node, aarch64, free VM -- do NOT use beep-node-a/beep-node-b, held by beep-hmj) that beep delivers type=LoadBalancer traffic under u7s v0.3.0-snapshot.1, with the leading root-cause fix applied: geneve0 pre-created + net.ipv4.conf.{all,geneve0}.rp_filter=0 on the node (beep-a5k's top suspect -- an address-less geneve0 fails rp_filter's loose-mode exception, silently dropping every decapped forward packet before cni0/veth, confirmed via beep's own scripts/smoke-k3s-controller.sh and scripts/e2e-lb-k3s.sh comments + a live kprobe:ip_route_input_noref trace). Also apply deploy/daemonset.yaml --pod-cidr=10.244.0.0/16 (u7s's real flannel CIDR, not the manifest's k3s-flavored 10.42.0.0/16 default) and use the real least-privilege deploy/rbac.yaml + a genuine X.509 client-cert kubeconfig Secret (not an admin cert, closing beep-a5k hypothesis 5). Since u7s's v0.3.0-snapshot.1 release assets are x86_64-only and beep-smoke is aarch64, build u7s from source at the v0.3.0-snapshot.1 tag rather than installing the prebuilt tarball. Assert: type=LoadBalancer Service reachable, real client IP delivered to the backend (not NAT'd/node address) -- matching the bar ai/extended-context/roadmap.md already sets for beep's own k3s/flannel e2e. Optional negative control: repeat once with rp_filter left at default (2) and assert the identical zero-response failure u7s observed, to prove the fix is necessary+sufficient, not just correlated. Cross-node is a stretch goal only if a second free VM exists later (not beep-node-a/-b).
notes:
Findings doc (beep-a5k) now specifies a 3-pass recipe to isolate two distinct code-confirmed mechanisms: pass 1 = deploy the manifest as-shipped (no --pod-cidr override) and dump POD_TARGETS/FLOW_TABLE on the backend node -- expect POD_TARGETS to lack the real pod IP and FLOW_TABLE to stay at 0 entries (controller/src/reconcile.rs:191-214's silent anti-spoof admission gate). Pass 2 = fix --pod-cidr + geneve0 + real RBAC, leave rp_filter at default -- expect FLOW_TABLE to populate but client still gets zero response (isolates the rp_filter mechanism). Pass 3 = add net.ipv4.conf.all/geneve0.rp_filter=0 -- expect 200 OK with the real client IP delivered. See the findings doc's (c) section for the full recipe.
LIVE-CONFIRMED on lima-node-smoke (u7s's own single-node Lima VM, not beep-smoke -- see deviation note below), 2026-09-16 ~09:00-09:22 UTC. All 3 passes reproduced their predicted signature; the rp_filter contradiction is DEFINITIVELY RESOLVED: single-node DOES need rp_filter=0, refuting scripts/smoke-remote.sh:151-158.

Pass 1 (as-shipped daemonset.yaml, pod-cidr=10.42.0.0/16, no geneve0): controller CrashLoopBackOff, "populating CONFIG map / resolving ifindex for geneve0 / No such device". bpftool map dump: POD_TARGETS=0, FLOW_TABLE=0. Confirms Gate 1 (compounded with the undocumented geneve0-precreate requirement).

Pass 2 (--pod-cidr=10.244.0.0/16 fixed, geneve0 pre-created, genuine least-privilege kubeconfig via the real CertificateSigningRequest API -- CN=beep-controller, kubectl certificate approve, NOT an admin cert -- closing hypothesis 5; rp_filter left at kernel default 2): controller Running 1/1, "all 3 hooks attached". POD_TARGETS=1 (10.244.0.7), VIP_MAP=1. status.loadBalancer.ingress=192.168.109.3. 3/3 curl from a genuine foreign client (separate Lima VM, lima-node-5, same L2 subnet, kube-proxy stopped/disabled) timed out with zero HTTP response. FLOW_TABLE=3 entries (one per attempt), same "return-path redirect record" shape u7s's own mayor-re973 round 5 captured cross-node. This is single-node (front==backend==192.168.109.3), same decap-to-veth hop round 5 exercised cross-node.

Pass 3 (added net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=0 + net.ipv4.conf.geneve0.rp_filter=0, no other change): the same 3 curl attempts now return HTTP 200. GET /clientip on the agnhost backend echoed 192.168.109.1:<port> -- the foreign client's REAL address, not NAT'd to the node/VIP address. Going from 3/3 zero-response to 200+real-client-IP with ONLY the rp_filter sysctl changed proves necessity+sufficiency on single-node.

ANSWER to the open contradiction: rp_filter is NOT cross-node-specific and NOT an artifact of smoke-remote.sh's synthetic lo-alias fixture -- it reproduces and is fixed identically on a single-node deployment with a real flannel-CNI pod veth. beep-o1b's fix scope must NOT be narrowed to cross-node-only; smoke-remote.sh:151-158's "a real deployment... does not appear to need this" claim is empirically refuted and should be corrected/removed.

Deviations from dispatch (Rule 7, flagging): used u7s's own lima-node-smoke VM (u7s's own established single-node-smoke naming/network convention, hardcoded in scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh's VM_NAME case statement) instead of literally beep-smoke, because beep-smoke's own Lima base image/cloud-init is incompatible with u7s's kubelet.yaml template (forcing --vm beep-smoke through u7s's own tooling would have required deleting and recreating beep's smoke VM under a different image). beep-node-a/beep-node-b were NOT touched despite the dispatch brief claiming all 3 VMs were free -- live evidence at session start (k3s server up 27min on node-a, k3s agent up 1d4h on node-b, plus concurrent-session artifacts in the shared scratchpad tasks dir) contradicted that claim, so I treated the more conservative bead-notes constraint (do not touch node-a/-b) as authoritative per Rule 11 (evidence over an unverified blanket claim). u7s-apiserver/scheduler ran on the Mac host with --port 16443/--kubelet-port 16250 (not defaults) to avoid colliding with a pre-existing Lima port-forward already bound to 6443/6444 on this shared host. beep-controller was cross-built from THIS repo's HEAD via `cargo +nightly zigbuild` (matching scripts/smoke.sh's own convention) rather than built natively on the VM.

No reusable repro script produced/PR opened: this was a one-shot manual verification (CSR-minting + ad hoc kubeconfig assembly are fragile, one-off steps not worth hardening into a permanent harness the way scripts/smoke.sh/smoke-remote.sh are for beep's own k3s substrate). All test K8s objects, the u7s host processes, and the 3 Lima VMs (lima-node-smoke, lima-node-5, beep-smoke) were torn down/stopped at the end; u7s and beep worktree git state confirmed unchanged (only pre-existing .beads/ai-dashboard housekeeping diffs, present before this session started).

title: release-machinery: tagging scheme (v*->:latest, main->:sha), auto-create GitHub Release on v*, fix versioning ADR daemonset-pin flaw
description: Operator decisions 2026-09-15. (1) TAGGING (delivery.yaml): v* tag push -> image :vX.Y.Z (immutable) + :latest, guarded so :latest only advances for the HIGHEST semver (a backport to an older line must not regress :latest). main merge -> :sha ONLY (drop the current main->:latest; NO mutable tip-of-main tag -- YAGNI, :sha covers exact-commit needs; only daemonset.yaml + the e2e rig consume today's :latest=main, both better on :sha/release). Current delivery.yaml: branch->:latest+:sha, v*->:version (not :latest); rework to the above. (2) AUTO-RELEASE (delivery.yaml): on a v* tag, auto-create the GitHub Release, body from docs/release-notes/<tag>.md, title=tag -- so the manual Release step (skipped for v0.1.0) can't be missed. Needs ; if docs/release-notes/<tag>.md is absent, fall back to --generate-notes rather than failing delivery. (3) DAEMONSET/ADR: daemonset.yaml STAYS :latest (no per-release pin). Fix docs/decisions/versioning.md: REMOVE the 'pin deploy/daemonset.yaml to :vX.Y.Z' cut step -- it's temporally impossible (pin commit lands after the immutable tagged commit, so the tagged commit never carries its own pin). Document: daemonset stays :latest (=newest release under the new scheme); users override to a version/sha via kustomize. Record that rationale. (4) De-draft docs/release-notes/v0.1.0.md (drop '(draft)/Not yet cut' -- v0.1.0 IS cut). (5) Update deploy/README if needed (kustomize-override note). NO VM needed (config+docs). title: docs(design): consolidate kube-proxy/flannel coexistence contract into a durable operator doc
description: The coexistence contract is scattered (ADR servicelb-ebpf-geneve-dataplane.md:46, design ebpf-lb-dataplane.md:88, deploy/daemonset.yaml comments) and the live PROOF lives only in mayor-waqhd's close note + a findings doc on an unmerged branch that gets pruned. Write docs/design/kube-proxy-coexistence.md stating: (1) verified kube-proxy mode(s) and the IPVS verdict from the live test; (2) DaemonSet-on-all-nodes as a hard coexistence rule (IPVS binds the VIP on every node); (3) VIP-disjointness contract -- pod-CIDR ENFORCED at startup (src/main.rs:195), Service-CIDR UNENFORCED (operator responsibility); (4) that the controller publishes the VIP via status.loadBalancer.ingress and beep's tc-ingress front-runs kube-proxy. notes: VERDICT from beep-03m (IPVS live test, 2026-09-15): IPVS-mode kube-proxy is INCOMPATIBLE with beep. Not the hypothesized kube-ipvs0 VIP-hijack (that's refuted: kube-ipvs0 skips a node's own VIP; tc-ingress fronts it regardless of mode). Actual cause: the controller publishes EVERY node's physical IP into the LB Service status.loadBalancer.ingress[], so under IPVS each node binds every OTHER node's real IP on its own kube-ipvs0 -> reciprocal duplicate-IP conflict that breaks node-to-node TCP (5x reproduced, 1 VM crash). iptables baseline PASSED before+after. title: test(k3s): verify beep coexistence with IPVS-mode kube-proxy (kube-ipvs0 VIP-hijack)
description: mayor-waqhd proved kube-proxy coexistence for IPTABLES mode ONLY (evidence was iptables-save; k3s defaults to iptables). Operator flagged the IPVS-mode conflict: IPVS kube-proxy binds every Service VIP (incl. status.loadBalancer.ingress IPs) to the kube-ipvs0 dummy device as a LOCAL address -> local REJECT of VIP traffic. beep's controller DOES publish the VIP into status.loadBalancer.ingress[].ip (controller/src/status.rs:75), which kube-proxy watches in both modes, so IPVS WOULD bind the VIP. Architecturally beep's tc/tcx-ingress classifier on eth0 (src/main.rs:246, ebpf/src/main.rs:817) front-runs the kernel routing/local-delivery decision, so the forward path SHOULD survive on a node where beep intercepts and the VIP is in VIP_MAP -- but this is UNTESTED in IPVS mode. Because IPVS binds the VIP on EVERY node, DaemonSet-on-all-nodes is a hard coexistence rule. GOAL: settle empirically whether beep works with IPVS-mode kube-proxy.
acceptance_criteria: A clear PASS/FAIL verdict on IPVS-mode coexistence with evidence: whether kube-ipvs0 binds the VIP; whether client->VIP->backend forward round-trip survives; whether east-west ClusterIP still returns 200; tc-interception evidence (bpftool net show, FLOW_TABLE growth for VIP only). Findings doc written + verdict recorded in the bead close note.
close_reason: FAIL, but not the hypothesized failure. kube-ipvs0 skips a node's own VIP (matches its real interface address) -- beep's tc-ingress still fronts it first regardless of proxy mode, refuting the local-REJECT hypothesis. The actual failure: beep's controller publishes every DaemonSet node's own physical IP into the same LB Service's status.loadBalancer.ingress[], so kube-proxy's IPVS reconciler binds each OTHER node's real address onto its own kube-ipvs0 as a local NOARP dummy-device address -- a genuine duplicate-IP conflict on beep's flat bare-metal network that broke node-to-node TCP connectivity (5x reproduced, incl. one full Lima VM crash), preventing a clean end-to-end round-trip test under live IPVS mode. DaemonSet-on-every-node scales the hazard: every node pair binds the other's address. Full evidence: ai/findings/2026-09-15-beep-03m-ipvs-coexistence.md (PR #69, adds a reusable --proxy-mode passthrough to scripts/k3s-up.sh). Feeds beep-2ej.

title: fix(controller): second malloc_trim(0) call after initial watch bootstrap settles
description: Audit beep-gcd (ai/findings/2026-09-14-beep-gcd-controller-rss-audit.md, lever #2): main.rs:264-267 calls malloc_trim(0) once, right after drop(ebpf) -- before parse_kubeconfig, build_tls_connector, and the three initial LIST responses are parsed. Any transient allocation peak from that later phase (JSON list-body parsing, DER/cert parsing, AWS-LC init buffers) is never handed back to the OS: glibc only releases heap memory via an explicit trim or when a freed chunk sits at the top of the heap above the trim threshold. The PR #57 idle-baseline RSS measurement (6948 kB) was taken after this untrimmed phase, so this cost may already be baked into the reported baseline. Add a second malloc_trim(0) call (same #[cfg(target_env = "gnu")] gate) once the initial Service/EndpointSlice/Node list-watch bootstrap settles (e.g. after on_nodes_listed's first apply_reconcile). Est. 0.1-0.3 MiB, low confidence, but essentially free and safe -- same call already used elsewhere in this file. Add a regression test or note in the doc comment for why the timing matters.
notes: Self-contained (beep-eyz measurement — ai/findings/2026-09-14-beep-eyz-controller-rss-dhat.md): MEASURED near-zero yield — recommend closing rather than implementing. dhat + a direct RSS trace on the real binary show the dominant transient peak in the whole controller lifecycle is NOT the kubeconfig/TLS/JSON-list phase this bead targets — it's aya/aya-obj parsing the kernel's BTF blob inside load_ebpf (17-31 MiB spike), which happens BEFORE the existing single malloc_trim(0) call and is already fully reclaimed by it (RSS trace: 22,132 kB peak -> 7,284 kB right after that call runs). The later phase this bead's second trim targets showed ZERO measurable RSS growth in a 9-second trace, and its total dhat-tracked allocator churn across the whole run (rustls+serde_json+hyper+tokio+clap combined) is under 1.4 MiB ever allocated, not simultaneously live. A second trim's ceiling is well under the original 0.1-0.3 MiB estimate, likely near 0. Source: bead beep-eyz.
close_reason: Measured near-zero yield (beep-eyz dhat profile, PR #63): the real RSS peak is the BTF-parse spike (~22MB→7MB) which the EXISTING malloc_trim at main.rs:264-267 already reclaims; the later phase a 2nd trim would target shows ZERO RSS growth over 9s. A second malloc_trim(0) buys nothing. Closing as verified-not-worthwhile.

title: feat(controller): drop aws-lc-rs, swap rustls crypto provider to a lighter backend
description: Audit beep-gcd found kubeconfig/Cargo.toml's plain `rustls = "0.23"` takes rustls's default features, which select aws-lc-rs -- a statically-linked C crypto library (AWS-LC, BoringSSL/OpenSSL-derived) built via cc+cmake, not a pure-Rust minimal backend. ring is already in Cargo.lock but only as rcgen's dev-dependency (test certs), never shipped in the release binary. Est. 1-3 MiB of the ~6.8 MiB idle RSS baseline (ai/findings/2026-09-14-beep-gcd-controller-rss-audit.md lever #1) -- the single largest actionable lever found. RISK: rustls-post-quantum's ML-KEM-768 hybrid key exchange is implemented via aws-lc-rs, not ring -- dropping aws-lc-rs means dropping post-quantum TLS to the apiserver entirely, a security-posture decision needing explicit operator sign-off before implementation, not a free swap. Needs a live Linux build+size/bloaty comparison to confirm the actual MiB delta (no VM was available for this audit).
notes:
Self-contained (beep-eyz measurement — ai/findings/2026-09-14-beep-eyz-controller-rss-dhat.md): dhat (Rust-heap tracer) CANNOT see aws-lc-sys's own C-level malloc() calls (its FFI wrapper aws-lc-rs's Rust-side code is the only part dhat instruments) — this bead's core estimate (1-3 MiB) is neither confirmed nor refuted by the dhat run. MEASURED instead: the Rust-visible slice of the whole TLS stack (rustls itself + aws-lc-rs's thin FFI wrapper) totals under 1 MiB ever allocated and ~117 KiB retained at idle across the run — nowhere near multi-MiB. If aws-lc-rs really costs several MiB, it is almost certainly compiled .text/.rodata code size and/or AWS-LC's own C-heap state, not anything a Rust allocator swap touches. Treat this as a disk/code-size question first, an idle-RSS question second — still needs its own size/bloaty binary comparison (as originally planned) before go/no-go on the post-quantum-TLS trade-off. Source: bead beep-eyz.
MEASURED (node-a, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, cargo build --release -p beep-controller): swapping rustls's crypto provider from aws-lc-rs to ring saves ~1.43 MiB (19.2%) on the unstripped binary (7,763,672 B -> 6,269,208 B) and ~1.25 MiB (23.2%) stripped (5,641,512 B -> 4,330,800 B); .text alone drops 1.19 MiB (5,445,965 B -> 4,194,505 B). cargo-bloat attributes 453.9 KiB of .text directly to aws_lc_sys (the compiled C library) plus 25.2 KiB to aws-lc-rs's Rust FFI wrapper -- confirms this is compiled-code size, consistent with beep-eyz's dhat finding that it is NOT an idle-RSS story. Dockerfile only COPYs the binary into debian:trixie-slim (no other build steps), so image-size delta tracks the binary delta directly (~1.3-1.5 MiB uncompressed layer; did not do a full docker build per task scope).

SECURITY CONFIRMED: rustls-post-quantum's ML-KEM-768 hybrid key exchange depends on aws-lc-rs and cannot link against ring at all -- removing aws-lc-rs means removing the rustls-post-quantum dependency entirely (confirmed by building the ring variant: it only compiles once rustls_post_quantum::provider() is replaced with rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider()). Result: apiserver TLS would negotiate classical-only key exchange (X25519/P-256 ECDHE), zero PQ hybrid groups offered -- not a degradation, a full removal of PQ-TLS.

RECOMMENDATION: operator's stated priority order is correctness > security > perf, and size is explicitly a resource-starved-cluster concern -- but ~1.3-1.5 MiB is a minor fraction of the debian:trixie-slim base image, while the security capability lost (PQ-TLS to the apiserver) is total, not partial. Given the stated priority order ranks security above perf/size, default recommendation is KEEP aws-lc-rs (keep PQ-TLS) unless the operator has a hard, already-binding image-size budget this measurably threatens. This is the operator's call -- bead stays OPEN pending that decision.

Verified clean: no Cargo.toml/source edits committed (all throwaway edits made on a disposable /home/lima.guest/beep-src copy on node-a, never on the tracked worktree); node-a repo copy, cargo-bloat, and /tmp binaries removed; node-a stopped. cargo fmt --check and cargo test -p beep-common (32 passed, 0 failed) run clean on the unmodified worktree.

title: bug(controller): early reconcile before Node LIST completes can wipe already-programmed VIP_MAP/TARGET_PORTS fronts on restart
description: Surfaced in PR #51 re-review (beep-v2c). controller/src/watch.rs:307 documents the empty-node_ips startup window as 'fail-closed self-healing', but that undersells it: reconcile::diff has delete-on-missing semantics, and the bpffs map pins SURVIVE controller restarts. So on restart, if a reconcile fires before the Node LIST completes (node_ips still empty → desired fronts = empty), the diff treats every already-programmed VIP_MAP/TARGET_PORTS front as 'to delete' and WIPES them -> transient traffic blackhole until the Node LIST lands and the next reconcile re-adds them. Self-healing but a real restart-time outage window. Fix: gate the front-programming reconcile on the Node LIST having completed at least once (or suppress delete-all when node_ips is empty-because-not-yet-listed, distinct from empty-because-no-nodes).
acceptance_criteria: A controller restart cannot wipe existing VIP_MAP/TARGET_PORTS fronts due to an empty-pre-LIST node set; a regression test covers the pre-LIST reconcile producing no destructive front diff.
notes: PR #53 fix-round: round-1 commit fa90d3a introduced a POD_TARGETS regression (the nodes_listed gate zeroed pod_targets, so apply_pod_targets full-synced pinned entries to empty on restart -- same blackhole class as this bug, reopened for pod targets). Fixed in commit 90d2522: pod_targets computed UNCONDITIONALLY in desired(), only the front (VIP_MAP/TARGET_PORTS) loop gated on nodes_listed. Round-2 review APPROVED (LGTM-with-suggestions). Residual NARROWER self-healing multi-node LIST-ordering recurrence filed as beep-j79. NB: this bead was closed after the first (buggy) commit; the fix landed later in the same PR #53.

title: spike(test): BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN tier scoped to REACHABLE hooks (uplink_ingress parse/VIP_MAP/DNAT wiring) — beep-ctc no-go only covered the unreachable geneve-decap branches
description:
Re-scope of the beep-ctc spike. beep-ctc returned NO-GO, but ONLY for its two named acceptance branches (pod-admission-drop + backend-src-port-remap), which both live inside try_geneve_decap_forward (ebpf/src/main.rs:591) -- reachable only via geneve_ingress after a bpf_skb_get_tunnel_key/_opt read that a synthetic BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN skb cannot supply. That no-go is correct for those branches but does NOT evaluate the REACHABLE hooks.

Why this matters: the dataplane has 4 classifier hooks. uplink_ingress (main.rs:373, the client's first packet on the client-facing NIC) does header-parse + load_direct offset math + EtherType/proto gates + VIP_MAP admission + DNAT rewrite -- NONE of which read tunnel metadata, so they ARE test_run-reachable. uplink_egress_return (main.rs:938) is gated on skb->mark (is_redirected_return_mark), which ctx_in CAN inject, so it is likely reachable too. beep-ctc's own DESCRIPTION listed exactly these parse/gate/rewrite paths as 'likely coverable' -- the acceptance criteria just happened to name two branches in the one unreachable hook.

CAVEAT (from beep-ctc, main.rs:52-54): the DECISION functions (decap_forward_pod_admission, resolve_backend_src_port, backend_port_resolution, egress_return_admission, is_redirected_return_mark, ...) are all imported from beep-common and are unit-testable there WITHOUT a kernel. So test_run must justify itself on the ebpf-side WIRING that beep-common cannot cover: load_direct offset arithmetic, map lookups (VIP_MAP/TARGET_PORTS/POD_TARGETS), and the actual rewrite OUTPUT BYTES + L4 checksum (rewrite_l4_port / DNAT). Offset-math and checksum bugs are precisely what beep-common decision-logic tests miss and only the e2e smoke catches today.
design: Spike-first, on beep-smoke (Linux-only). STEP 1: enumerate the ebpf-side wiring in uplink_ingress (and, if quick, uplink_egress_return) that has NO beep-common equivalent and is currently covered ONLY by the e2e smoke -- if everything meaningful is already in beep-common, that is a fast NO-GO, record it and stop. STEP 2: prototype ONE reachable end-to-end assertion via aya SchedClassifier::test_run() -- e.g. feed a valid client TCP packet with a pre-populated VIP_MAP entry, assert verdict + the mutated packet bytes show correct DNAT (dst rewritten, L4 checksum fixed); or a negative (dst not in VIP_MAP -> passthrough, no rewrite). STEP 3: go/no-go on whether this wiring coverage earns a Linux-only CI job. If GO: a small test_run tier covering the 2 highest-value reachable branches, wired into the Linux CI path (not the macOS cargo-test step).
acceptance_criteria: A documented go/no-go recorded on this bead, grounded in WHICH reachable-hook wiring is genuinely uncovered by beep-common today. If go: a working test_run harness exercising at least 2 reachable uplink_ingress verdict/rewrite branches (asserting mutated-packet output bytes, not just a verdict code), wired into the Linux CI path.
notes: GO/NO-GO SPIKE RESULT: NO-GO. uplink_ingress never rewrites the packet at all -- no DNAT, no checksum fixup -- so the acceptance bar (assert mutated-packet output bytes show correct DNAT) is unsatisfiable on this hook. Read try_uplink_ingress_headers (ebpf/src/main.rs:402) end to end: on a VIP_MAP hit it parses headers, mints FWD_PENDING, calls bpf_skb_set_tunnel_key/_opt (encap metadata), and bpf_redirects -- it never touches the packet's own IP/port bytes. The actual DNAT (rewrite_ip_port, line 790, with checksum fixup) lives exclusively inside try_geneve_decap_forward (line 591), gated behind bpf_skb_get_tunnel_key/_opt -- the hook beep-ctc already proved unreachable via test_run. Prototyped src/bin/spike_test_run.rs (cross-built via cargo-zigbuild, run on beep-smoke, same kernel 6.8.0-138-generic as beep-ctc): a VIP_MAP-hit packet returns verdict=7 (TC_ACT_REDIRECT) with data_size_out=54 bytes_equal_to_input=true (i.e. UNCHANGED bytes, confirming no DNAT here); a VIP_MAP-miss packet returns verdict=0 (TC_ACT_OK), also unchanged. bpf_skb_set_tunnel_key/_opt (SET, unlike GET) do NOT fail on a synthetic skb -- new information vs beep-ctc. bpftool map dump on FWD_PENDING after the hit run showed the correct flow-key + VipBackend value threaded through map-lookup-into-map-insert wiring. So mechanics work and SOME wiring genuinely has no beep-common equivalent (load_direct offsets, VIP_MAP lookup, FWD_PENDING insert-if-absent, tunnel-key/opt set calls) -- but all of it is verdict/map-content-only, not byte-mutation, and is mostly redundant with what scripts/smoke.sh's e2e round trip already proves transitively (a broken VIP_MAP hit already fails the smoke outright). The one real gap -- FWD_PENDING's insert-if-absent affinity pin has no beep-common decision function and no smoke fixture exercises a mid-flow VIP_MAP value change to catch a regression -- is real but narrow, and cheaper to close via a multi-backend smoke fixture or a beep-common extraction than via a new kernel-version-sensitive BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN CI job. Cost (new Linux-only CI job, kernel-sensitive test_run semantics, packet-fixture upkeep) doesn't earn its keep given beep's pre-alpha/simplicity-first stance. Prototype code discarded before commit (same precedent as beep-ctc); beep-smoke VM state cleaned (bpftool map show confirmed no beep maps left loaded). Full writeup: ai/findings/2026-09-11-beep-4lo-reachable-hook-spike.md
close_reason: NO-GO recorded on bead notes; findings committed at ai/findings/2026-09-11-beep-4lo-reachable-hook-spike.md (commit 2ab7645, pushed to worker/agent-ab481144a909e12c9). No PR: uplink_ingress performs no DNAT rewrite at all (that lives exclusively in the unreachable geneve-decap hook per beep-ctc), so the acceptance bar's byte-mutation assertion is unsatisfiable here; remaining verdict/map-content coverage is mostly redundant with scripts/smoke.sh's e2e round trip and doesn't earn a new Linux-only CI job.

title: net/servicelb: containerd default AppArmor profile blocks bpffs writes for the controller DaemonSet (CAP_BPF/CAP_NET_ADMIN insufficient)
description:
Discovered by beep-s5k's controller-driven k3s round-trip gate: the
servicelb-controller DaemonSet (deploy/daemonset.yaml) crashloops on every
node before loading a single eBPF program.

ANSWER: containerd's default `cri-containerd.apparmor.d` profile (applied
automatically to every non-privileged pod on an AppArmor-enabled host,
confirmed loaded via dmesg) denies ALL writes under the bpffs mount
(/sys/fs/bpf), including plain mkdir/touch, even as UID 0 with
CAP_BPF+CAP_NET_ADMIN added. Linux capabilities and AppArmor are separate
confinement layers -- capabilities don't grant AppArmor-mediated file
access. Confirmed empirically:
  - `mkdir /sys/fs/bpf/beep` inside the pod -> EACCES (Permission denied)
  - controller's own `create_dir_all` -> `Error: creating pin dir
    /sys/fs/bpf/beep\n\nCaused by:\n    Permission denied (os error 13)`
  - pre-creating the dir on the HOST (outside the container) does not
    help: a plain `touch` under it from inside the pod still EACCES
  - setting `container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/<container>:
    unconfined` on a debug pod with the SAME securityContext immediately
    fixes both mkdir and touch

This blocks mayor-9gr0n's controller from ever running under k3s's
(containerd's) default confinement, and is very likely to affect ANY
containerd-managed cluster with AppArmor enabled (not Lima/k3s-specific).

NOT FIXED in beep-s5k: loosening a privileged hostNetwork DaemonSet's
AppArmor confinement is a security-posture decision needing explicit
operator sign-off, not something to bake into deploy/daemonset.yaml from
an agent session -- Claude Code's own auto-mode classifier declined to
apply `appArmorProfile: {type: Unconfined}` live, flagging it as a
security weakening. See ai/findings/2026-09-11-beep-s5k-controller-apparmor-bpffs-block.md
for full evidence and options.

OPTIONS (operator decision needed):
  (a) securityContext.appArmorProfile.type: Unconfined on the container --
      simplest, broadest.
  (b) author + ship a custom Localhost AppArmor profile scoped to exactly
      the bpf()/mount/bpffs surface beep-controller needs -- narrower,
      more work, needs the profile loaded on every node out-of-band.
  (c) investigate a containerd/k3s config change that exempts CAP_BPF-
      holding pods from the default profile cluster-wide.

Verification: once decided and applied, beep-s5k's gate

title: Evaluate BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN as a middle test tier for beep-ebpf branch wiring
description:
Decide whether to add a BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN (aya program.test_run()) harness as a middle test tier between 'cargo test -p beep-common' (pure logic, any host) and the 2-node smoke round trip (scripts/smoke-*), and introduce one if it earns its keep.

Why: the branch-wiring in ebpf/src/main.rs -- given a beep-common decision, does each arm call the right helper -- has no unit test today; it is covered only by the full 2-node e2e round trip. test_run feeds a hand-crafted packet buffer into a SINGLE loaded program in ONE Linux VM and returns the verdict code plus the mutated packet bytes (and maps can be pre-populated and dumped), so it could cover a real slice of that gap at lower cost than a topology.

Likely coverable by test_run: header parse + load_direct offset math + EtherType/proto gates; admission map gating (pre-populate POD_TARGETS/VIP_MAP/TARGET_PORTS, assert TC_ACT_SHOT vs TC_ACT_OK on hit/miss -- specifically the pod-admission-drop branch in try_geneve_decap_forward and the backend-src-port remap branch); DNAT/un-DNAT checksum rewrites (assert output bytes + checksum).

Likely NOT coverable, stays e2e-only: tunnel metadata + redirect helpers (bpf_skb_set_tunnel_key/_opt, bpf_redirect, bpf_skb_change_head/_type) -- these only do anything inside a live datapath with real netdevs/tunnel device.

Open question the eval must answer: the middle tier ADDS coverage but would NOT shrink the smoke suite (the live-kernel bug history in main.rs is almost entirely tunnel/redirect, which still needs the round trip). So this is a spike-first task: is the added parse/gate/rewrite coverage worth the harness's maintenance cost? Runs on a Linux kernel only (Lima/CI path, not cargo test on macOS).
design: Spike first, implement only on a 'go'. Investigate aya's TestRunOpts/program.test_run() for tc SchedClassifier programs: can it accept a synthetic skb, honor pre-populated maps, and return the mutated packet + verdict. Prototype against ONE branch (pod-admission-drop) before generalizing.
acceptance_criteria: A documented go/no-go decision with rationale recorded on this bead. If go: a working test_run harness that exercises at least the pod-admission-drop and backend-src-port-remap verdict branches, wired into the Linux CI path (not the macOS cargo-test step).
notes: GO/NO-GO SPIKE RESULT: NO-GO. Do not build a BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN harness. Prototyped probe classifiers calling bpf_skb_get_tunnel_key (geneve_ingress's VNI dispatch) and bpf_skb_get_tunnel_opt (the pod_ip read gating the pod-admission-drop check in try_geneve_decap_forward), run via aya program.test_run() on beep-smoke (Linux 6.8.0-138-generic aarch64): bpf_skb_get_tunnel_key returned -22 (EINVAL), bpf_skb_get_tunnel_opt returned -2 (ENOENT), both on a synthetic test_run skb. Both helpers read ip_tunnel_info/metadata_dst attached by the real Geneve receive path, state BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN never populates and TestRunOptions::ctx_in cannot inject (struct __sk_buff has no tunnel-key field). Consequence: geneve_ingress always exits TC_ACT_OK before reaching try_geneve_decap_forward, and even a direct test-only call into that function hits tunnel_opt's unconditional TC_ACT_SHOT before the pod-admission-drop gate or backend-src-port-remap logic ever runs -- both acceptance-criteria branches are structurally unreachable, not just the tunnel/redirect write helpers already flagged e2e-only. The pure decision logic in both branches already lives in beep-common and is unit-tested via cargo test -p beep-common with no kernel needed; a test_run harness could only add wiring coverage, which is exactly what's unreachable. Cost (new Linux-only CI job, kernel-version-sensitive semantics, fixture upkeep) buys nothing extra and does not shrink the smoke suite. Prototype code discarded before commit. Full writeup: ai/findings/2026-09-11-beep-ctc-testrun-spike.md
close_reason: NO-GO recorded on bead notes; findings committed at ai/findings/2026-09-11-beep-ctc-testrun-spike.md (commit 0627f31, pushed to worker/agent-a33bed5cc28229f1c). Acceptance criteria satisfied: documented go/no-go decision with rationale.

title: build(perf): build controller in CI with rust-cache + COPY binary into a slim image (replaces in-image build)
description: The delivery image build (root Dockerfile, built by .github/workflows/delivery.yaml with cache-to/from: type=gha) recompiles the rarely-changing third-party crate set (~4 min: registry download + dep compile) on EVERY run, because the dependency compile shares a Docker layer with the source COPY -- any source change busts it. Restructure the Dockerfile so cargo dependencies build in a SEPARATE, cacheable layer keyed on Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, so the existing gha layer cache reuses it across runs. RECOMMENDED: cargo-chef (prepare -> recipe.json -> cook builds only deps; workspace-aware; produces real layers gha-cache persists). MUST preserve: the eBPF cross-build (build.rs/aya-build needs bpf-linker + pinned nightly + rust-src -- the chef/cook stage must carry that toolchain), the checksum-verified bpf-linker fetch (beep-vk5), dual-arch (amd64+arm64), and a minimal runtime stage. FALLBACK if cargo-chef conflicts with aya-build's cross-compile: BuildKit registry+target cache mounts, but then verify gha-persistence actually works (it often doesn't) -- surface to mayor if neither cleanly works.

Better cache reuse per operator: build beep-controller in CI with Swatinem/rust-cache (~/.cargo + target, keyed on Cargo.lock) -- reuses far more than Docker layer cache for Rust AND lets us build per-arch WITHOUT the current ~37min QEMU emulation -- then the image just COPYs the prebuilt binaries into a minimal base. Dual-arch: prefer cargo-zigbuild cross-compiling both x86_64+aarch64 on one amd64 runner (matches smoke.sh's existing cross-build) OR native ubuntu-24.04-arm runner. GLIBC-COMPAT: prefer STATIC MUSL (x86_64/aarch64-unknown-linux-musl -> distroless/scratch, no glibc dep; mirrors the musl-static bpf-linker); RISK = aws-lc-sys (rustls via beep-kubeconfig) + musl can be finicky -> fall back to glibc build w/ runtime base glibc>=builder, surface the choice.
