title: design(servicelb): per-flow backend affinity pinning + endpoint-removal conntrack eviction (Phase 5)
description:
Phase 5 needs one coherent decision on flow-to-backend affinity: the forward
path must pin a backend per flow rather than re-resolving VIP_MAP per packet,
AND endpoint removal must selectively evict the conntrack entries that point
at the departed pod. These pull in opposite directions and cannot be designed
separately.

Two problems, one decision:

1. No per-flow backend affinity. uplink_ingress chooses the backend from
   VIP_MAP on every forward packet at servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:227, and
   FWD_FLOW only records which node the packet went to for the return-path
   existence check at line 496, where the value is read and discarded (see
   aie31.20). With today's one-static-backend fixture this is invisible. With
   real multi-endpoint Services in Phase 5, repointing a VIP mid-connection
   immediately moves live traffic to a backend that holds no TCP state for
   it, breaking the connection. Real load balancing needs the backend chosen
   once per flow and stored in conntrack, with later packets following the
   stored choice. That is what conntrack affinity is for, and the current
   shape does not do it.

2. No selective eviction on endpoint removal. When a pod leaves the
   EndpointSlice, established flows pinned to it are orphaned. kube-proxy
   actively flushes conntrack for a removed endpoint, which matters most for
   UDP, which has no teardown to age the entry out. The eBPF equivalent is a
   targeted pass that deletes FWD_FLOW and REV_FLOW entries pointing at the
   removed pod. This is a deliberate scoped delete, not a reset, and it is
   missing.

The tension: affinity pinning says do NOT disturb a live flow on an unrelated
config change, while eviction says DO disturb the specific flows whose
backend is gone. The decision has to state exactly which config changes
disturb which flows, mirroring kube-proxy's terminating-endpoint and
graceful-termination semantics.

Invariant this rests on, now recorded in aie31.8: reconciliation is a live
per-key map write to VIP_MAP and POD_TARGETS, NOT a program reload or a
process restart, so it never by itself resets the LRU conntrack maps. The
orphaning above is semantic, not a map reset.

Overlaps aie31.10, since keying the eviction pass needs a richer POD_TARGETS
than one port per pod. Phase 5 scope, mayor-9gr0n.

DONE WHEN: a written decision defines the per-flow affinity model and the
exact set of config changes that trigger selective conntrack eviction, with
UDP called out explicitly.
notes: IMPLEMENTATION now tracked in epic beep-03i (operator 2026-09-19: eviction is a FIRM v1 production-readiness requirement). This bead is the DECIDED design; beep-03i builds it. beep-5lw (multi-pod LB) depends on beep-03i.

title: design(servicelb): unified flow table with an explicit role tag
description:
Merge FWD_FLOW and REV_FLOW into one table discriminated by an explicit tag
rather than by address disjointness, and settle the ceiling as part of it.

Measured on a live kernel via bpftool, so these are exact rather than
modelled. All LRU_HASH, bytes_memlock:

  forward map today, key 37 value 4, 8192 entries        918,400
  reverse map today, key 37 value 12, 8192 entries       983,936
  pair today                                           1,902,336
  unified, key 38 value 12, 4096 entries                 492,416
  unified, key 38 value 12, 8192 entries                 983,936
  unified, key 38 value 12, 16384 entries              1,966,976

The CI sampler total across all five servicelb maps is 1,909,072, leaving
6,736 for CONFIG, VIP_MAP, and POD_TARGETS.

The tag byte is free. BPF rounds key_size up to a multiple of 8 when sizing
elements, confirmed by measurement rather than by reading hashtab.c: key
sizes 36 through 40 all cost the same, and 41 jumps by exactly 8 bytes per
entry. See bd memory ebpf-map-key-size-rounds-up-to-8 for the numbers and the
reproduction method. That is why the unified 8192 row above is byte-identical
to today's reverse map on its own.

Alternative worth weighing and recording: the tag does not strictly need a
38th byte. The existing proto byte holds 6 or 17 and has six spare bits, so a
high bit could carry direction and a second bit QUIC, keeping the key at 37
and touching no call sites. The explicit byte is recommended anyway, since it
costs nothing and is self-documenting, but the choice should be written down.

Do NOT rest this on VIP-space versus pod-CIDR disjointness. That invariant
does not hold for hostNetwork Pods; see the disjointness bead. Note also that
the two maps carry different value types today, 4 bytes against 12, so the
tag has to select the value shape as well as the key population.

Capacity tradeoff to decide, not assume. Unifying at 8192 halves memory and
keeps full capacity for a single-role node, but halves worst-case capacity
for a node serving both roles. Unifying at 16384 costs 64,640 bytes more than
today and yields 16384 flexible slots instead of a fixed 8192 plus 8192,
which strictly dominates. Bucket arrays round to a power of two, so those are
the only sensible stops.

QUIC folds in as a third population under the same tag once native QUIC
lands, rather than needing a fourth map.

Also update ai/extended-context/ebpf-lb-dataplane.md line 96, which states
the key as 37 bytes.

DONE WHEN: one tagged table exists, its value shape covers both roles, and
the ceiling choice is recorded with its reasoning.
notes: DECIDED 2026-09-09 (operator): use an EXPLICIT TAG BYTE (approach A) -- a 38th key byte discriminating forward vs reverse entries in the unified table. Rationale: FREE (BPF rounds key size up to a multiple of 8; keys 36-40 cost the same memlock, measured live), self-documenting, and decoupled from the proto byte. NOT approach B (packing direction into spare proto bits). The merge uses this explicit discriminator, NOT VIP-vs-pod-CIDR address disjointness -- that's the whole point (relates to the tavxy misdelivery class). Entry-count/ceiling is settled during implementation and feeds aie31.23 (re-tighten the map-memory ceiling). DISPATCH TIMING: it's an ebpf/src/main.rs change -- dispatch only after PR #9 (f3ru5) merges, so the ebpf/ hot surface is free and this builds on the merged change_head fix. When dispatched, record this decision in the PR body too (mayor method: decisions live in bead notes AND the merging PR).
close_reason: PR #10 opened: unified FWD_MAIN+REV_FLOW into FLOW_TABLE (38-byte tagged key, 16384 entries), FWD_PENDING untouched. Verified on beep-smoke (smoke.sh + assert-ebpf-map-memory.sh) and cross-node (smoke-wg-2node.sh).

title: perf(servicelb): release the aya object after attach so the DaemonSet idles thin
description:
Pin the maps, drop the aya Ebpf object after attach, trim the heap, and
reopen maps from their pins when they are next needed, so the DaemonSet
container idles thin instead of holding load-time state forever.

The blocking loop at src/main.rs:204 is correct and must stay. A DaemonSet
Pod only accepts restartPolicy Always, so exiting would be restarted and
eventually backed off. The cost is not the sleep, it is what the process
holds while sleeping. Ebpf::load parses the object at line 153 and keeps the
BTF, relocation state, and program registry alive for the whole process
lifetime, and the 214 KiB embedded blob is resident once touched. Glibc does
not return that heap on its own, so resident memory sits at the load-time
high-water mark, which in a container is what the memory request has to cover
on every node.

MapData::from_pin exists in aya 0.14 for reopening. Phase 5's watcher needs
map handles, not the parsed ELF.

Worth recording while here: since Linux 5.11, BPF map memory is charged to
the creating process's cgroup, so the roughly 1.82 MiB of map memory counts
against this container's own memory limit rather than sitting outside it. Map
sizing and container limits are one budget, not two. The bump_memlock_rlimit
call at src/main.rs:296 only matters for kernels older than that.

DONE WHEN: steady-state RSS in the existing loader-rss.csv sampler drops
measurably below the load-time peak, with the attachment still live.
close_reason: PR #13 opened. Steady-state RSS 19936-19940 KB (baseline) -> 19840-19860 KB (fixed), consistent ~90KB/0.45% drop, non-overlapping across 7 runs on beep-node-b; scripts/smoke.sh --vm beep-node-b PASS confirms attachment survives the Ebpf drop.

title: perf(servicelb): make the per-packet flow-table writes conditional
description:
Replace the unconditional per-packet map inserts with
lookup-then-write-on-miss.

servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:238 inserts into FWD_FLOW on every forwarded
packet, and line 418 inserts into REV_FLOW on every decapped packet, not just
on the first packet of a flow. An LRU hash update takes the bucket
raw_spinlock and can run the LRU shrink path. A lookup is an RCU read that
already refreshes the entry's LRU reference bit, so recency is preserved
without the write. The difference is largest under multi-core load, where
several CPUs serialize on one bucket lock for a single busy flow.

FWD_FLOW's value is constant per flow, so skipping the rewrite is trivially
safe. REV_FLOW's value can legitimately change if the ingress node changes,
so the check there is exists-and-matches rather than plain existence.

DONE WHEN: steady-state packets of an established flow take the read path,
verified by a map-update counter that stays flat while traffic flows.
close_reason: PR #14 opened

title: perf(servicelb): gate the egress conntrack lookup on POD_TARGETS membership
description:
Gate the uplink-egress conntrack lookup on POD_TARGETS membership, checking
only that the source address is a backend Pod on this node and deliberately
not comparing the port.

try_uplink_egress_return at servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:537 performs a
40-byte-key LRU hash lookup on every TCP and UDP packet leaving the node
before it can reject non-ServiceLB traffic. POD_TARGETS is a 32-entry map
with a 4-byte key, so probing it first is a far cheaper hash and it
short-circuits before the 37-byte key is even built on the stack.

Membership only, not a port match. Comparing the packet's source port against
the current POD_TARGETS value would couple the return path to a value that
can change under it during a rolling update or a targetPort change, dropping
live flows whose reverse entry was written under the old port. The current
code cannot produce that failure, because it matches purely on the stored
tuple. Membership is safe by construction: a flow only has a reverse entry if
the forward path found its pod in this map, so anything still live passes,
and a pod absent from the map is going away regardless.

Pairs with the REV_FLOW-miss bead, which needs exactly this positive
identification before it can safely turn a miss into a drop.

DONE WHEN: traffic not sourced from a backend Pod rejects without touching
the conntrack table, and a test covers that a targetPort change does not
break an in-flight flow.
close_reason: PR #1624 opened

title: perf(servicelb): direct packet access instead of bpf_skb_load_bytes on both uplink hooks
description:
Replace ctx.load with direct packet access on both uplink hooks, because
every ctx.load is a bpf_skb_load_bytes helper call and these hooks see all
node traffic, not just ServiceLB's.

Confirmed in aya-ebpf 0.2.1: TcContext::load delegates to SkBuff::load, which
calls bpf_skb_load_bytes. Cost per packet before either hook can even reject
non-ServiceLB traffic:

- try_uplink_egress_return, servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:537. Seven helper
  calls plus a 40-byte-key LRU hash lookup.
- try_uplink_ingress, servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:207. Five helper calls plus
  a VIP_MAP lookup.

That is paid by kubelet, etcd, image pulls, flannel, and everything else
entering or leaving the node. ctx.data and ctx.data_end are available in this
aya version, turning each read into a plain load behind one bounds check.
Adjacent fields can also coalesce: the source and destination addresses are
contiguous, as are the two ports.

Caution: direct packet access covers the linear head only. Headers are linear
in practice for tc ingress and for egress from a local socket, but any read
that reaches into a payload, which native QUIC will need for the DCID,
requires bpf_skb_pull_data or a load-bytes fallback.

This gets more valuable under the dual-stack and QUIC requirements, not less.
IPv6 means branching on ethertype with different header offsets and walking
extension headers, each of which is another helper call under the current
approach.

DONE WHEN: header reads go through ctx.data and ctx.data_end with
verifier-accepted bounds checks, and the servicelb smoke fixture still passes
end to end.
close_reason: PR #15 opened

title: docs(ebpf-lb): correct the VIP-space vs pod-CIDR disjointness claim
description:
The claim that VIP-space and the pod CIDR are disjoint by construction is
false for hostNetwork Pods, and the doc uses it to justify a design choice.

ai/extended-context/ebpf-lb-dataplane.md line 89 states the two ranges never
collide and concludes that one map per protocol can cover both the forward
and reverse roles. A Pod with hostNetwork true has a pod IP equal to its node
IP, which is exactly VIP space under the node-owned-address model. That is
standard Kubernetes semantics, not misconfiguration, and this repo already
ships two hostNetwork DaemonSets in manifests/kube-proxy.yaml and
manifests/flannel.yaml. The doc specifies the servicelb control plane itself
as hostNetwork at line 131.

Concrete collision, node N at 192.168.109.3. A forward key for a service
fronted at N holds N's address in its other-address slot. A reverse key for a
hostNetwork backend on N holds the same address in the same slot. A client
legally reusing one local port across both makes the two 37-byte keys
byte-identical.

The ranges are also only disjoint by configuration today, not by
construction. The pod CIDR is 10.244.0.0/16 from scripts/install.sh:890 and
node addresses sit on 192.168.x.x, set by unrelated mechanisms with no
cross-validation. The --vip-ip flag at src/main.rs:56 is an unvalidated
address with no check that it is the node's own or outside the pod CIDR.

Calibration note: the same paragraph of this doc was already wrong once,
specifying LRU_PERCPU_HASH, which was empirically disproved and corrected.
That is reason to audit the neighbouring sentence rather than defer to it.

Consider merging with aie31.3, which corrects the map type and footprint in
the same file. Kept separate here because this one also needs a code change.

DONE WHEN: the doc states the real constraint rather than a false invariant,
and the loader rejects a VIP that falls inside the pod CIDR.
close_reason: Doc correction landed in PR #1614; loader-side validation (also required by this bead's done-when) is out of scope for this doc-only PR and tracked separately as mayor-aie31.24

title: net/servicelb: Tier-1 eBPF smoke harness -- load + verifier-accept + single round-trip (local-gated)
description:

title: net/servicelb: userspace controller -- watch type=LoadBalancer Services + EndpointSlice, program dataplane maps
description:

title: design(servicelb): aie31.21 eviction ignores cross-node convergence drift - delivery node must be the authoritative consistency point
description: Operator raised 2026-09-07: the aie31.21 affinity+eviction doc reasons about eviction as a per-node reconcile but never addresses the cross-node convergence WINDOW. Each node's DaemonSet processes the same EndpointSlice event at different times (uplink latency), so node eBPF state can drift apart for multiple seconds before converging. Governing principle to add to the doc: dataplane is eventually-consistent per node; correctness must NOT depend on synchronized updates; worst case during the window must be bounded transient drop/hang, NEVER misdelivery to a wrong live pod. Scenarios: new-flow selection divergence = safe (per-flow ECMP-sticky to one ingress node); stale FWD_FLOW pin during removal lag = blackhole/hang if IP not reused (bounded, ok) BUT misdelivery if the departed pod's IP is reused before the lagging ingress node evicts (UNSAFE - the drift window widens this). RESOLVING INVARIANT: make the delivery (backend-host) node validate each inbound Geneve-decap packet against its OWN current serving-set for the front IP before delivering - the host has a lag-free view of its local pods, so ingress drift degrades to a drop at the authoritative node, not a cross-service leak. OPEN QUESTION to verify against code: does the inbound decap-forward delivery path in crates/servicelb/servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs currently do this membership check? aie31.14 gates EGRESS on POD_TARGETS (different hook) - may not cover inbound delivery. Action: amend aie31.21 doc with the cross-node-drift section + invariant; file a build bead if the delivery-side validation is missing. Part of parked aie31 epic.
notes: Verdict: invariant does NOT hold today. try_geneve_decap_forward (servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:331-471) trusts the ingress-stamped Geneve pod_ip unconditionally and DNATs to it; its only check, TARGET_PORTS.get(front tuple) (main.rs:361-368), validates "this node serves some backend for this front", not "this pod_ip is a current member" -- no analogue of aie31.14's egress POD_TARGETS-membership gate exists on the inbound decap-delivery path. Drift verdict: new-flow divergence is SAFE (per-flow ECMP-sticky); stale FWD_FLOW pin without IP reuse is SAFE (bounded blackhole/hang); stale pin WITH pod-IP reuse before the lagging ingress evicts is UNSAFE -- misdelivers to the new pod, and the drift window directly widens this exposure. Doc amended: ai/findings/2026-09-06-mayor-aie31.21-affinity-pinning-eviction.md, new "Cross-node convergence & drift" section (keeps its aie31.21 header, doc-only PR under mayor-1dwwz). Build follow-on filed: mayor-tavxy (P2, parent aie31, cross-refs aie31.21 + aie31.14). Left OPEN per dispatch instructions -- operator resolves aie31.21 separately.
close_reason: Deliverable verifiably done: cross-node convergence-drift invariant documented (aie31.21 doc drift section) and the build-side fix landed as mayor-tavxy / PR #11 (decap-delivery validates target pod against local serving-set). Remaining aie31.21 affinity/eviction coupling is tracked in aie31.21 itself; no separate open work here.

klipper-lb-alike, mayor-0gpqp, already closed). kube-proxy stays untouched
for east-west ClusterIP/NodePort traffic; this epic owns north-south

(written once this epic's ID is known). Child beads filed one per phase,

(superseded), mayor-mma08.

Adopting Flannel in the harness too would make it CONSUME node.spec.podCIDR like prod, which activates #1525/#1527's podIP-allowlist in conformance and closes mayor-elmno's test-fidelity gap for free. See mayor-elmno notes for the full evidence (two-allocator drift breaks the allowlist on any non-default VM) + the consume-model refactor recipe if Flannel-uniform isn't chosen.
CLARIFICATION 2026-09-04: Phase 4 mayor-lrbvo deploys the eBPF for its go/no-go gates via the MANUAL Phase-1 loader mayor-g6u8s with static fixture maps, NOT the Phase-5 DaemonSet mayor-9gr0n -- the DaemonSet is production-only and Phase 4 blocks it, so it cannot exist yet. See lrbvo notes for the full reasoning. Prevents mis-reading Phase 4 as requiring Phase 5 first.
filed 13 improvement/safety/investigation beads from the 2026-09-05 servicelb footprint review, aie31.8 through aie31.20. P1: aie31.8 map pinning, restart currently loses all flow state; aie31.9 REV_FLOW miss forwards a pod-source packet unencapsulated; aie31.10 POD_TARGETS holds one port per pod, blocking multi-port Services in Phase 5; aie31.11 flow-table admission control, the table is cyclable by 8192 unauthenticated packets. P2: aie31.12 disjointness doc fix, false for hostNetwork Pods; aie31.13 direct packet access, 7 helper calls per egress packet today; aie31.14 egress POD_TARGETS membership gate; aie31.15 conditional map writes; aie31.16 slim the resident loader; aie31.17 unified tagged flow table. P3: aie31.18 remap probe trims, aie31.19 DWARF strip, aie31.20 stateless Geneve MAC. Measured baseline via bpftool on a live kernel: FWD_FLOW 918400 plus REV_FLOW 983936 = 1902336 of the 1909072 sampler total; unified at 8192 entries = 983936, a 48 percent cut, with the tag byte free because BPF rounds key_size up to a multiple of 8. See bd memory ebpf-map-key-size-rounds-up-to-8.

Doc consolidation (axzsf) records the decisions into extended-context/ADRs, does the VIP rename, deletes the stale bguco findings doc. One open sub-question: dksf5 TCP-eviction yes/no.

title: servicelb: complete IPv6-underlay support -- geneve_ingress GET-side peer attestation reads remote_ipv4 only; verify set_tunnel_remote v6 SET-arm on a live v6-underlay rig
description: From critical review of PR #118 (2026-09-19). Two v6-UNDERLAY gaps, both DORMANT today (every current deployment runs a v4-only underlay regardless of inner-packet family): (1) geneve_ingress peer attestation (NODE_ALLOW / is_known_peer GET side) still reads the outer tunnel source as remote_ipv4 only -- a genuine v6 underlay peer would not be attested. (2) set_tunnel_remote's v6 SET arm (outer Geneve tunnel-remote for a v6 node address) is reasoned from net/core/filter.c source, not empirically confirmed -- no live v6-underlay rig exists. DISTINCT from beep-7qm.7 (which exercises inner-family diversity over a v4-only underlay, never this GET-side branch). Blocked on a real v6-underlay test rig. Parent: beep-7qm (IPv6 epic, IPv6-only underlay half).

title: code-quality: audit + reduce unsafe blocks across loader/ebpf/common
description: Operator (2026-09-19): the codebase carries a large amount of unsafe; investigate whether it can be effectively reduced. SCOPE INTO the v1.0 code-quality-audit phase (roadmap: IPv6 -> real-hardware -> perf+code-quality audit -> security audit -> docs) -- NOT now. The audit should separate irreducible-unsafe (inherent to eBPF/aya direct packet access, map ops, raw pointer casts across the kernel/user boundary; netlink/libc FFI in the loader -- justify + document + tighten invariants) from reducible-unsafe (wrap in safe abstractions, prefer aya's safe APIs where they exist). Deliverable: a findings doc quantifying unsafe blocks by category + a reduction plan. Part of the v1.0 epic beep-xfa.

title: servicelb: selective per-interface rp_filter — keep loose RPF on the uplink, disable only on geneve0 (harden plain-client-spoof path)
description: Researcher-validated 2026-09-18 (from operator's beep-ztb line of questioning). disable_rp_filter() (src/lib.rs:265, loops over [all, iface]) sets conf/all/rp_filter=0 node-wide, which ALSO removes the reverse-path check on plain (non-Geneve) client traffic arriving on the physical uplink at the LB front IP -- a hostile LAN host can spoof a plain client source with no kernel backstop. FEASIBLE FIX: conf/all=0 (floor, needed for decap) + conf/geneve0=0 (decapped packets re-enter ip_rcv_finish_core ON geneve0 per beep-n24, so need it off there) + conf/<uplink>=2 (loose RPF). Plain client traffic on the uplink then sees max(0,2)=2; decapped traffic on geneve0 sees max(0,0)=0. Both iface names are at the call site (controller/src/main.rs:275-277). The geneve-rp-filter-disable.md rejection of per-interface scoping (lines 26-36) was for the geneve0-only/all=default model, NOT this all=0+asymmetric-uplink model, so it does not block this. NEEDS a short ADR documenting why the prior rejection does not apply. FOLD INTO beep-1vf's disable_rp_filter() rework (same function, both one-time node-prep). SECURITY: hardens vs off-segment/implausible spoofed sources on the uplink; does NOT stop same-L2 spoofing (WireGuard remains the closer, #106). eBPF-RPF alternative (bpf_fib_lookup, Cilium-style) considered: same routing-check semantics, more hot-path code, and does NOT eliminate the /proc write because decap traverses the kernel receive path (TC_ACT_OK, ebpf/src/main.rs:880); only a redirect-based decap (beep-hy2) could remove the sysctl entirely. Ref beep-ztb, beep-1vf, beep-hy2.
notes: CORRECTION (2026-09-18): anti-spoof value is MARGINAL on a single-uplink ingress node. rp_filter (strict OR loose) cannot catch a spoofed EXTERNAL client IP -- it routes back via the same uplink and passes; rp_filter only catches topologically-implausible sources (internal/pod-range, other-segment, martians). So beep-hl6 does NOT meaningfully close the plain-client-spoof gap -- WireGuard remains the real closer (#106). beep-1vf's minimal fix keeps the CURRENT all=0+geneve0=0 set (no uplink re-raise; that IS today's behavior, proven by smoke.sh). beep-hl6 = optional narrow hardening (uplink=1 strict, and only if symmetric routing) -- likely not worth the config surface; revisit with multi-NIC/asymmetric topology or as part of beep-hy2.

title: harden k3s :sha rig: verify sed image-override matched, docker rmi cleanup, rust-src prereq check

title: ci: assert embedded eBPF object has no .debug_* sections and stays under a size ceiling (guard DWARF-strip from silent revert)
description: Flagged by critical-reviewer on PR #104 (mayor-aie31.19, which added the DWARF strip in build.rs). Nothing in CI or scripts/test-* asserts the embedded beep-ebpf object stays free of .debug_* sections or under a size ceiling, so a future accidental revert of the strip step in build.rs would silently reintroduce ~270KB of DWARF bloat with no CI signal -- the exact regression class aie31.19 was created to prevent, one layer out. Add a CI assertion (natural home: extend the memory-smoke job alongside assert-ebpf-map-memory.sh, or a small build-artifact check) that the embedded object has zero .debug_* sections and is under a size ceiling (post-strip ~46KB; ceiling e.g. 100KB). LOW severity, coverage gap not a defect. Ref PR #104 review pullrequestreview-5246901294. Related: beep-bfy (CI-wire Rule-14 shell tests) -- both CI-hardening, could be done together.

title: docs(decisions): ADR for NODE_ALLOW startup-blackout security-vs-availability tradeoff (fronts_known gating)
description: Reviewer suggestion on beep-bwh/#98 (pullrequestreview-5244341782): gating NODE_ALLOW on the cluster-wide fronts_known signal accepts a WIDER Geneve blackout window on controller cold-start/node-join in exchange for restart-wipe safety (NODE_ALLOW is VIP_MAP-shaped/cluster-wide; narrowing to pod_targets_known would wipe already-pinned peer entries mid-Node-LIST). Write a short ADR (docs/decisions/, ~400w, from _template.md) recording the SETTLED tradeoff; reference beep-ur2 (narrowing improvement) + beep-ztb (open load-bearing-vs-defense question) as out-of-scope/open. title: Decide whether Geneve underlay isolation is load-bearing or defense-in-depth for NODE_ALLOW
description:
Follow-on to beep-bwh/#98. NODE_ALLOW (outer Geneve tunnel-source attestation) is defense-in-depth under a WireGuard transport (WG peer-auth already attests the outer source before eBPF runs) but load-bearing under an Ethernet-direct underlay (rp_filter=0 removes the kernel backstop, no host firewall ships, port 6081 is open to anything routing to the node's physical IP).

Open question from the design audit: is the Geneve underlay's L2/L3 segment already isolated (dedicated VLAN, no untrusted host reachability) in the intended bare-metal deployment, making NODE_ALLOW pure defense-in-depth -- or is an adversarial host on that segment part of beep's actual threat model, making NODE_ALLOW load-bearing and possibly insufficient alone (e.g. needing option C, a host firewall/ipset, in addition)? Needs the operator's deployment-topology answer, not more code-reading -- and, once answered, either an ADR recording the assumption or a follow-on to add a host-firewall layer.

Ref beep-bwh, PR #98, ai/findings/2026-09-18-beep-bwh-antispoof-design.md open question 3 (deleted from main once beep-bwh's follow-ons are filed).

title: feat(ebpf+controller): NODE_ALLOW multi-homed/NAT node support -- admit all of a node's reachable IPs
description: Follow-on to beep-bwh/#98 (operator decision 2026-09-18: track, don't block v1). #98 ships NODE_ALLOW keyed on ONE IP per node (node_ips.values(), the recorded Geneve-endpoint address). A multi-homed/NAT'd node whose actual Geneve outer-source IP differs from that single recorded address is DROPPED by the drop-on-miss gate. Operator accepted single-IP-per-node as the v1 constraint. This bead: extend NODE_ALLOW + controller population to admit ALL of a node's reachable addresses (K8s Node.status.addresses) so multi-homed/NAT nodes work; add a cross-node test; resolves the reachability audit's open NAT/multi-homing question. Ref PR #98.

title: ci/ruleset: controller-cross-aarch64 gates only via mayor-tick, not branch protection — decide required vs advisory
description: From PR #87 (beep-pw4) critical-review, MED. The new controller-cross-aarch64 job (+ the dhat-heap guard step) is NOT in main-branch ruleset 22605658's required_status_checks (which lists only test-gate/lint-gate/memory-smoke/fmt) nor behind any needs: gate in ci.yaml. So a RED aarch64/dhat result does not block a merge at GitHub's branch-protection layer — it blocks only because scripts/mayor-tick.sh treats any failed/pending statusCheckRollup entry as blocking before queuing. Effective for the mayor-driven flow; the gap is a non-mayor merge path. DECISION (operator/admin): (a) add controller-cross-aarch64 to required_status_checks (true gate, +~2min every PR), or (b) keep advisory and soften the 'PR-gate' framing in the bead/docs. beep-pw4's description said to coordinate with beep-5jb (owns the required-check set) if touching it. Cross-ref PR #87.

title: bare-metal anti-spoof hardening: validate outer Geneve tunnel source against known peer nodes (compensating control for rp_filter=0)
description:
No validation exists today: beep_ebpf's geneve_ingress only checks tkey.tunnel_id (VNI_FWD/VNI_RET) and the inner packet's fields; the outer tunnel's source address (tkey.remote_ipv4, read at ebpf/src/main.rs:781 as ingress_node_ip) is trusted as-is and never checked against a list of known peer node IPs. Confirmed by reading ebpf/src/main.rs's geneve_ingress/try_geneve_decap_forward/try_geneve_decap_return: no NODE/peer allowlist map exists in beep-ebpf or beep-common.

This matters more now that beep-o1b lands rp_filter=0 node-wide: any host that can reach a node's Geneve UDP port with a guessable/known VNI and a Geneve option matching a currently-programmed VIP:PORT/pod_ip can inject a decap-forward packet claiming any client source IP -- rp_filter=0 removes the kernel-level backstop that would otherwise drop an asymmetric-return packet, and there is no beep-level check to replace it.

Proposed compensating control: tunnel-endpoint attestation -- gate geneve_ingress's decap on the outer packet's actual source IP (available via the skb, not just tkey.remote_ipv4) matching a known-peer-node set (from the controller's own Node watch), dropping otherwise. Needs design: where the peer-node set lives (new map, POD_TARGETS-adjacent), whether to check the *outer* IP header directly vs relying on tkey fields, and interaction with NAT'd/multi-homed node networking.

Cross-ref beep-o1b (rp_filter=0 decision + this gap identified during its investigation), beep-hy2 (routing-based decap escape hatch -- a different, more expensive way to avoid needing rp_filter=0 at all).

Out of scope for beep-o1b: check-only per that bead's brief; this bead is the place to actually build it.
notes: Findings doc: ai/findings/2026-09-18-beep-bwh-antispoof-design.md (audit branch worker/agent-a2b657c7). Reachability confirmed (research 2026-09-18): geneve0 binds 0.0.0.0:6081 (src/lib.rs:223, 'type geneve external'). WG-transport mode: outer source cryptographically attested by WireGuard peer-auth (AllowedIPs) BEFORE eBPF -> NODE_ALLOW redundant/defense-in-depth. Ethernet-direct mode (eth0 uplink; design commits to 'four underlays, none assumed' ebpf-lb-dataplane.md:16-18): 6081 reachable by any host routing to node phys-IP, no crypto filter, rp_filter=0 -> spoofable; NODE_ALLOW load-bearing. Pure-eth (eth0->eth0) is design-intent but UNTESTED (no smoke rig; see beep-or9). No host firewall shipped (6081 open). Return path try_geneve_decap_return does NO source check today (_tkey unused, ebpf/src/main.rs:839). Decision pending operator: A (eBPF map) / C (host firewall) / defer.
close_reason: PR #98 opened: NODE_ALLOW peer-node attestation for Geneve decap

title: controller: IPVS-mode kube-proxy incompatibility — publishing every node IP into LB ingress causes reciprocal kube-ipvs0 duplicate-IP conflict
description: ROOT CAUSE found by beep-03m live test (PR #69 findings). beep's controller publishes EVERY DaemonSet node's own physical IP into the same LoadBalancer Service's status.loadBalancer.ingress[] (controller/src/status.rs). Under IPTABLES-mode kube-proxy this is benign. Under IPVS-mode kube-proxy, each node's IPVS reconciler binds each OTHER node's real address onto its own kube-ipvs0 as a local NOARP dummy address -> on a flat bare-metal L2 network that is a genuine reciprocal duplicate-IP conflict: broke node-to-node TCP (k3s control-plane tunnel 'connection reset by peer', 5x reproduced causally; one full Lima VM crash). NOTE: the originally-feared 'kube-ipvs0 hijacks a node's own VIP -> local REJECT' does NOT occur (kube-ipvs0 skips an IP that matches the node's own real interface addr; beep's tc-ingress fronts it regardless of mode). DECISION for operator (fix vs document): (A) v0.1.0 = document IPVS-mode as UNSUPPORTED (use iptables/nftables) via beep-2ej [pragmatic, iptables is the tested+default mode]; (B) v1.x = change the controller's ingress-publication model so it does not make every node claim every other node's IP [real design work]. Filed P3 as v1.x-hardening; escalate to P2 only if we commit to IPVS support. Gated by non-default IPVS mode.
acceptance_criteria: Either (A) docs/design/kube-proxy-coexistence.md (beep-2ej) states IPVS-mode kube-proxy is unsupported with the duplicate-IP rationale, OR (B) the controller no longer publishes all node IPs into every node's LB ingress such that IPVS-mode no longer produces the reciprocal conflict (re-verified via scripts/k3s-up.sh --proxy-mode ipvs).
notes: DECISION (operator 2026-09-15): PATH A — document IPVS-mode kube-proxy as UNSUPPORTED for v0.1.0 (via beep-2ej); the controller ingress-publication redesign for IPVS support is DEFERRED to v1.x. This bead stays open as the v1.x redesign tracker; beep-2ej carries the doc. Recorded in beep-2ej's PR body per mayor decision-record rule.

title: bug(controller): backend Pod on a late-ordered Node in the startup LIST can have POD_TARGETS wiped until that Node's event lands
description: Surfaced in PR #53 round-2 review (beep-k48 fix). pod_targets_for_node's result in desired() depends transitively on self.node_ips via the endpoint->node_ip resolution filter (controller/src/watch.rs:401). on_node fires apply_reconcile once per Node-LIST item BEFORE on_list_complete flips nodes_listed (main.rs:169-176, watch.rs:513-523). In a multi-node cluster a backend Pod hosted on a Node ordered LATER in the LIST response is filtered out of pod_targets (its node_ip not yet known), and the unconditional POD_TARGETS full-sync (apply.rs:88) wipes its pinned entry until that Node's own event lands. A narrower, self-healing recurrence of beep-k48's blackhole class, NOT covered by beep-k48's tests. Fix direction: defer the destructive POD_TARGETS full-sync (or the per-node endpoint filter) until nodes_listed, or make pod_targets resolution independent of the incremental node_ips during LIST. Regression test: multi-node LIST ordering with the backend's node last.

title: fix(hygiene): worktree-hygiene.sh exits 1 with no anomaly message on a clean repo; step E bead-ID parse only matches mayor-* not beep-*

(1) SPURIOUS EXIT 1: with a valid --live-agents and a verifiably-clean repo (no stray branches/worktrees; both worktrees legitimately live-or-open-PR), the script exits 1 while printing NO '[hygiene] ...' anomaly line -- just the git fetch output. There is no explicit 'exit 1' in the script (grep confirms only the two arg-error 'exit 2's), so it is a set -e / last-command-exit-status leak, not an intended anomaly signal. Effect: the 60m hygiene cron reports a non-zero 'anomaly' the mayor cannot act on (no message says what). (2) step E bead-ID parse gap: bead_id_from_finding() (scripts/worktree-hygiene.sh:294) greps only 'mayor-[a-z0-9.]+', so its stale-findings detection silently skips every findings doc whose header is 'Bead: beep-*' (this project's current prefix) -- step E is a no-op for beep-* findings. Fix: (a) make the script exit 0 when no anomaly was actually reported (guard the leaking command / accumulate an explicit anomaly count and exit on that), and (b) widen the bead-ID regex to '(mayor|beep)-[a-z0-9.]+'.
acceptance_criteria: worktree-hygiene.sh exits 0 on a clean repo with valid --live-agents (no spurious exit 1); any non-zero exit is accompanied by a printed '[hygiene]' line naming the anomaly; bead_id_from_finding matches beep-* IDs; a regression test in scripts/test-worktree-hygiene-logic.sh covers both (clean-repo-exits-0 and a beep-* stale-finding gets detected).

title: port(hygiene): --no-live-workers flag from litehop/u7s worktree-hygiene.sh (replace __none_live__ placeholder)
description:
Port the --no-live-workers flag from litehop/u7s's scripts/worktree-hygiene.sh into beep's copy of the same script, so the zero-workers hygiene tick has a first-class affirmative flag instead of the __none_live__ placeholder hack.

WHY: beep's scripts/worktree-hygiene.sh (main() argv parse, ~L318-348) accepts only --live-agents <ids> and refuses outright when the normalized set is empty. Every worktree-hygiene cron tick with zero live workers (the common case) therefore has to pass a fake --live-agents __none_live__ placeholder. beep was imported from the u7s monorepo (u7s@4f898a4d) and u7s's copy has since diverged and added a proper flag for exactly this.

WHAT u7s DOES (verified 2026-09-10 via gh api repos/litehop/u7s/contents/scripts/worktree-hygiene.sh): --no-live-workers is an affirmative alternative to --live-agents for the zero-workers case; it is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with --live-agents (passing both refuses with a distinct message); a bare empty --live-agents "" with no --no-live-workers fallback still refuses. In u7s: no_live_workers flag var in main(), mutual-exclusion check, then the empty-set guard falls through only when neither is set.

SCOPE (Rule 2/3 -- keep it tight): port ONLY the --no-live-workers flag + its argv parse + mutual-exclusion guard + refusal-message update. u7s's script has ALSO grown a STEP A (its refusal message reads 'STEP A/C/D are destructive'); beep's only has STEP C/D. Do NOT wholesale-sync the script -- adapt the ported message to beep's STEP C/D wording, and leave the STEP A divergence alone (separate concern, out of scope here).
design: Source of truth: litehop/u7s scripts/worktree-hygiene.sh (fetch current via gh api repos/litehop/u7s/contents/...). Adapt STEP A/C/D refusal wording to beep's STEP C/D. Worker must run the script's own test harness on macOS (this is a bash script, no Linux/VM needed).
acceptance_criteria: scripts/worktree-hygiene.sh --no-live-workers runs the destructive steps on a zero-worker tree (exit 0); --live-agents "" (empty) still exits 2; passing BOTH --live-agents <ids> and --no-live-workers exits with a mutual-exclusion error; a regression test in the script's test file covers all three cases (fails if the flag or a guard is reverted); the 60m worktree-hygiene cron-loop prompt and the 'hygiene-script-empty-live-agents' bd memory are updated to prefer --no-live-workers over the __none_live__ placeholder.
notes: RECURRENCE (2026-09-11): scripts/worktree-hygiene.sh exits 1 even on a VERIFIABLY CLEAN repo (no worktrees/local/remote worker branches) when invoked with the --live-agents __none_live__ placeholder (the documented no-live-workers path). Effect: the 60m hygiene cron reports a false anomaly on every tick where no workers are live, training the mayor to ignore its exit code. The --no-live-workers flag port should make the empty/placeholder case exit 0 when nothing needs cleaning.

title: servicelb-ebpf: dual-role node's ungated reverse writes can LRU-evict a forward entry from the shared FLOW_TABLE
description: Accepted residual of aie31.17's flow-table merge (PR #10), flagged by the reviewer as needing its own bead. FWD_PENDING stays a separate admission-gated tier, but merging FWD_MAIN+REV_FLOW into one FLOW_TABLE means the reverse role -- which has NO admission gate -- shares capacity with forward entries. On a DUAL-ROLE node (ingress AND backend), a large reverse-write burst could LRU-evict a forward (admission-gated) entry. Failure mode is AVAILABILITY (the forward flow re-mints), NOT misdelivery. Reviewer + operator ACCEPTED shipping without a gate because: it's honestly documented (ebpf/src/main.rs:269-270 + design doc + PR #10 body), unreachable by current smoke fixtures (the anti-flush flood never completes a forward-decap, so never produces reverse-tagged writes), and triggering it needs overlay-internal positioning (a materially higher bar than the off-path spoofing the FWD_PENDING split defended). REVISIT with a reverse-side admission gate or per-direction capacity split IF dual-role nodes become a real deployment target. Ref: PR #10 review pullrequestreview-5152918958.
notes:
Re-anchor (2026-09-10, post #10/#14): STILL-HOLDS but it is a DOCUMENTED, DELIBERATELY-ACCEPTED trade-off, not an undiscovered bug. Reverse-tagged FLOW_TABLE writes (ebpf/src/main.rs:807-810) are ungated (write on first backend-decap, no admission gate); forward entries (:906-914) ARE gated (require return-leg promotion). On a dual-role node the shared 16384-entry LRU means a reverse-write burst can LRU-evict an established forward entry -- impossible pre-#10 when FWD_MAIN/REV_FLOW were separate maps; #14 PortMemo (3rd slot) slightly worsens occupancy. FAILURE MODE = availability (evicted flow re-mints on next packet), NOT misdelivery/correctness. Explicitly documented + accepted in the FLOW_TABLE comment (:275-310) and PR #10 review (pullrequestreview-5152918958) as a large-burst-only, dual-role-only concern. Fix options: A) gate reverse writes behind admission (per-packet cost, risks dropping legit return traffic); B) partition table by direction tag; C) per-direction sizing knob (mirror --fwd-pending-max-entries); D) status quo (what #10 chose). RECOMMENDATION: DEFER unless dual-role deployments become a near-term target -- availability-not-correctness, rare, already documented, and the fix is not free.
DECISION (operator 2026-09-10): ACCEPT the tradeoff; defer the code-side fix (reverse-write admission gate / partition / separate-maps) until it causes ACTUAL data loss. Rationale: availability-only (evicted forward flow re-mints on next packet, never misdelivery), dual-role node + large-burst only. Follow-on: load-test to find + document the safe concurrent-outgoing-flow burst threshold as a known operational limit (filed separately).

title: fix(ebpf): drop (not pass) a half-mutated skb when EtherType store fails after change_head

title: test-rig: eth0/user-v2-ingress cross-node smoke -- host client -> node-a VIP -> geneve-over-wg0 -> node-b backend
description:
GOAL: a 2-node smoke variant where the client arrives on node-a's ETHERNET (user-v2/Lima NIC) ingress -- NOT on wg0 -- and beep encapsulates over wg0 as the cross-node transport to node-b. Topology: host client -> (Lima port-forward) -> node-a user-v2 VIP:port -> beep tc-bpf ingress (uplink-iface = the user-v2 NIC, e.g. eth0/lima0, confirm inside the VM) -> bpf_redirect into geneve0 -> geneve OUTER packet routes to node-b over the wg0 underlay -> node-b decaps -> backend (nc -l serving 'OK') responds -> round trip back to the host client.

WHY: (1) more realistic than the existing wg-2node rig, where node-b doubles as its own client and the ingress uplink is wg0 (10.99.0.2:19100). Here the client is a real external origin (the macOS host via a Lima port-forward to node-a's VIP) and the backend is a genuinely separate node. (2) This is the multi-KIND path from beep-eix (eth0-in, wg0-out) -- exercises it as a TEST even before full multi-interface support, since single-interface eth0-ingress already works. (3) It is INDEPENDENT of the f3ru5 blocker: f3ru5 is the wg0-AS-INGRESS L3 redirect drop; here ingress is Ethernet (mac_len=14) so the redirect-into-geneve0 works. => testable NOW, before f3ru5 lands.

SETUP (sketch, adapt from scripts/smoke-wg-2node.sh + smoke-wg-2node-remote.sh): keep the wg0 tunnel + geneve0 collect-metadata setup between node-a/node-b; change node-a's beep --uplink-iface to the user-v2 NIC (was wg0); expose node-a's VIP to the host via a Lima port-forward (lima/beep.yaml or 'limactl forward'); drive the client with curl from the macOS host instead of from node-b's root netns; assert body 'OK' + dump geneve0/wg0 counters + bpftool map dumps on failure (same evidence as the existing rig).

CAVEAT: this sidesteps f3ru5 on the FORWARD INGRESS leg only. The RETURN leg (node-b -> node-a -> client) may surface its own L3/mac_len issue depending on how the reverse path egresses -- characterize it, don't assume full green. Reachability confirmed feasible: lima user-v2 gives VMs host-unroutable IPs, but a port-forward to node-a's VIP is a legitimate external-client stand-in (delivers to the Ethernet ingress; does NOT bypass the wg0 transport).

XREF: beep-eix (multi-interface feature this tests), mayor-f3ru5 (wg0-ingress path this is independent of), existing scripts/smoke-wg-2node.sh (wg0-ingress rig to adapt from).
design: P3, near-term testable (independent of f3ru5). A distinct rig from the wg0-ingress smoke, not a replacement. Value: realistic external-client + separate-backend topology; exercises the eth0-in/wg0-out multi-KIND path.
acceptance_criteria: A host-originated request to node-a's user-v2 VIP completes a cross-node round trip (geneve encap over the wg0 underlay, node-b backend responds 'OK') and the rig asserts it; on failure it dumps geneve0/wg0 counters + VIP/conntrack map dumps. Forward-ingress leg proven; return-leg behavior characterized (pass or documented blocker).
notes:
FINDING (rig built, PR #20): forward leg NOT proven end-to-end -- structural blocker, not a rig bug, so bead stays OPEN per dispatch brief.

Mechanism proven: VERIFIER-ACCEPT on both nodes (--uplink-iface eth0 confirmed as node-a's real Lima user-v2 NIC), FWD_PENDING minted on node-a for the client SYN, geneve0 TX/RX packet counts match exactly node-a->node-b, node-b's decap+DNAT writes the correct reverse conntrack entry.

Blocker: with only 2 assigned VMs and node-b required to host the backend, the client is necessarily node-b's own root netns (same reason smoke-wg-2node uses this convention -- a synthetic/foreign client address does not survive Lima's user-v2 virtual switch, confirmed via a standalone veth+forwarding test). `ip route get <node-b's own address>` on node-b unconditionally resolves to `local ... dev lo` -- the kernel can never select the Geneve-transport uplink (wg0) as the return leg's egress device for a destination that is the node's own address, regardless of eBPF logic or sysctl changes. Confirmed via /proc/net/snmp (TCP PassiveOpens on node-b never increments) and trace-cmd (decap'd packet dropped at tcp_v4_rcv+0x98 reason: NO_SOCKET).

Same class of problem as beep-n24 (client co-located with backend node), for the wg0-ingress rig -- this investigation additionally establishes WHY it's structural (the local-route short-circuit) rather than just a martian-source/sysctl issue. Real fix needs a 3rd VM (client address genuinely foreign to node-b), out of this bead's assigned 2-VM scope.

Also ruled out (investigated, evidenced): a literal macOS-host client via Lima port-forward. Lima's automatic port-forward dials the guest's OWN loopback address from inside the guest netns (never reaches eth0 tc-ingress); `limactl tunnel`'s SOCKS bridge accepts the CONNECT but delivers zero bytes/packets to the target's eth0.

RE-VERIFIED (2026-09-10, PR #20 branch worker/agent-afce641d5eacf8caa, live re-run on beep-node-a/b): NOT a rig-config bug and NOT a dataplane DNAT bug -- the already-documented structural client-colocation blocker, confirmed with fresh evidence, plus one correction to the earlier characterization.

Three data points line up exactly (no rig misconfiguration):
- geneve0 capture (pre-eBPF-DNAT, kernel Geneve decap only): inner SYN src=192.168.104.14:45980 dst=192.168.104.13:19100 (still the VIP, as expected before the tc hook runs).
- VIP_MAP/TARGET_PORTS/POD_TARGETS dumps on node-b: front 192.168.104.13:19100/tcp -> backend_node_ip 10.99.0.4, pod_ip 198.51.100.60, target_port 18090 -- all correct.
- `ss -tlnp`: nc alive, LISTEN on 198.51.100.60:18090 (TCP/IPv4) -- matches target_port exactly.

CORRECTION to the "forward SYN dropped NO_SOCKET" phrasing: lo capture during a fresh repro shows nc's OWN kernel emitting a genuine SYN-ACK from 198.51.100.60:18090, proving the decap'd+DNAT'd forward SYN DOES reach nc's real LISTEN socket (a NO_SOCKET drop cannot produce a SYN-ACK). A parallel trace-cmd -e skb:kfree_skb capture across a repeat attempt recorded zero kfree_skb events -- no NO_SOCKET drop fired this run. What actually breaks is the SYN-ACK's return: since its dst (192.168.104.14:45980) is node-b's own address, the kernel's local route sends it back via `lo` instead of wg0/geneve0, where it arrives with src=198.51.100.60:18090 -- not a match for curl's SYN-SENT socket (which expects a reply from 192.168.104.13:19100) -- so node-b's own stack RSTs it immediately. Same root cause the existing notes already named (client-colocation local-route short-circuit), just pinned to the exact packet that dies.

Verdict: no fix applied, none needed -- this is the environmental 2-VM-topology limit already on record, not a regression. Real fix still needs a 3rd VM. Bead stays OPEN/scope-blocked as before.
close_reason: Scoped deliverable complete: the eth0/user-v2-ingress cross-node rig landed via PR #20. Forward-ingress leg PROVEN end-to-end (client SYN -> decap+DNAT -> nc's real socket -> genuine SYN-ACK, captured on lo) and return-leg behavior CHARACTERIZED as a documented blocker (2-VM client-colocation -> return SYN-ACK routes via lo -> RST). Meets the bead's acceptance ('forward-ingress proven; return-leg characterized -- pass or documented blocker'). The full green round trip is owned by beep-vuh (3rd client VM, Phase 2), which folds in this rig.

title: feat(loader+ebpf): support multiple uplink + relay interfaces (not a single --uplink-iface)
description:
GOAL: beep must support MULTIPLE interfaces, not the single --uplink-iface it has today. Example node: eth0 (public internet) + wg0 (WireGuard) + eth1 (VPC-local). 'External' clients can arrive on eth0 OR wg0, and return/relay traffic may need to egress over eth1 OR wg0. Two dimensions: (a) multiple INGRESS uplinks admitting client traffic; (b) multiple EGRESS/relay interfaces for the outbound leg (new -- today the return path is single-uplink).

CURRENT SINGLE-INTERFACE LIMITS (interface audit over PR#3-era code):
- src/main.rs:76-82 -- --uplink-iface + --geneve-iface are single-valued String (default eth0/geneve0), NOT repeatable.
- src/main.rs:331-356 -- attach loop hardcodes 3 tc-bpf hooks all on the ONE uplink + geneve iface.
- src/main.rs:277-284 & ebpf/src/main.rs:253-263 -- Config holds a SINGLE uplink_ifindex + SINGLE uplink_l2_hlen, written once at load (src/main.rs:372-396); every eBPF redirect (ebpf/src/main.rs:283,644,737) reads that single value.

STRUCTURAL CHANGES (scope sketch, not final design):
- Repeatable --uplink-iface + a way to designate relay/egress interface(s).
- Config redesign: multiple ifindices with a PER-INTERFACE uplink_l2_hlen -- critical, since eth0 is L2/Ethernet (hlen=14) and wg0 is L3-only (hlen=0); they cannot share one value.
- Attach loop over N uplinks.
- eBPF redirect logic keyed on the INCOMING interface (currently assumes one), plus egress-interface SELECTION for the relay leg.

RELATIONSHIP: the wg0-uplink path must work end-to-end first (blocker mayor-f3ru5: L3-only wg0 -> Ethernet-type geneve0 redirect drops in-kernel; leading BPF_ADJ_ROOM_MAC fix DISPROVEN 2026-09-09). Multi-interface is broader/orthogonal, but any wg0 case inherits f3ru5. Not a hard dep.
design: Operator decision 2026-09-09: FUTURE feature, P3, not a blocker to anything now -- bump only if it becomes a blocker later. Subtlety to preserve: per-interface L2 header length (Ethernet 14 vs L3-only 0) must be per-uplink, not a single Config field.
acceptance_criteria: Loader accepts >1 uplink and >=1 designated relay/egress interface; Config carries per-interface ifindex+l2_hlen; tc-bpf hooks attach across all uplinks; eBPF admits client traffic on any configured uplink and selects the correct egress interface for the relay leg; single-uplink behavior unchanged as a subset.
notes:
SCOPE CLARIFICATION (operator 2026-09-09): this bead is COUNT, not KIND. It covers supporting MULTIPLE interfaces SIMULTANEOUSLY -- repeatable --uplink-iface, attach loop over N uplinks, Config with multiple ifindices, redirect keyed on the incoming iface, egress-iface selection. It is DISTINCT from supporting multiple KINDS of interface (L2 Ethernet hlen=14 vs L3-only like wg0 hlen=0), which is needed even for a SINGLE-interface / single-node bind and is delivered by mayor-f3ru5 (make an L3-only wg0 uplink work at all: synthesize a 14-byte L2 header via bpf_skb_change_head, gated on l2_hlen==0). f3ru5 is the PREREQUISITE that makes per-interface l2_hlen meaningful; beep-eix adds the many-at-once orchestration on top. Do not conflate KIND (f3ru5, even single-interface) with COUNT (this bead).
Cross-node-test relevance (operator 2026-09-10): once multi-uplink lands (eth0 ingress + wg0 transport simultaneously), the macOS HOST can be the cross-node test client via eth0 -- an alternative to the 3rd VM (beep-vuh) for the client-address-non-local-to-backend requirement. Near-term fix is the 3rd VM; host-as-client is the longer-term path this feature unlocks.
MULTI-IP / NODE_ALLOW facet (folded from superseded beep-5ng, 2026-09-18): once a node has multiple interfaces/IPs (this bead's eth0+wg0+eth1 example), the NODE_ALLOW peer-attestation gate added by beep-bwh/#98 -- keyed on ONE node IP (node_ips.values()) -- must be extended to admit ALL of a peer's reachable addresses (K8s Node.status.addresses), else a peer's Geneve outer-source arriving on a secondary interface is dropped. Controller-population + map-keying facet, distinct from this bead's loader/eBPF packet-path scope but the SAME multi-interface reality. Cross-ref beep-bwh/#98, beep-ztb, reachability audit's NAT/multi-homing question.
RATIFIED (operator 2026-09-19): MVP = multi-SYMMETRIC-uplink; repeatable --uplink-iface accepted. Return leg egresses via the INGRESS uplink (symmetric) -- FLOW_TABLE stores ingress ifindex; NO asymmetric egress-iface selection in MVP. Config gains a per-uplink {ifindex, l2_hlen} array in beep-common (Ethernet hlen=14 vs L3-only wg0 hlen=0). Single-uplink stays a subset. DEFERRED out of MVP: asymmetric relay/egress selection; NODE_ALLOW multi-IP admission (beep-5ng). Next: ADR + decomposition under beep-xfa.
SPIKE beep-eix.1 VERDICT (2026-09-19): multi-symmetric-uplink design VALIDATED on beep-smoke -- both feasible, no verifier blocker. Q1: one loaded SchedClassifier attaches to N uplinks (same prog_id via N TCX links). Q2: verifier accepts reading skb->ingress_ifindex as a HashMap<u32,Config> key + bpf_redirect on the result (context-struct field, NOT packet-data -> not the aie31.13 gotcha); live UDP round-trip confirmed. DECOMPOSITION NOTE: .3/.4/.5 are best done as ONE coherent PR -- the shared-Config change breaks both consumers at once and pre-alpha break-freely means no transitional shim to split them cleanly. Footguns filed to .3/.4/.5. Spike doc: branch worker/agent-adaf790811c615883 @ 7d07c4d (ephemeral, no PR; substance lifted into beads).
MVP MERGED (#112, 2026-09-19): multi-SYMMETRIC-uplink shipped -- repeatable --uplink-iface, per-uplink UplinkConfig map, ingress-ifindex-keyed admission, symmetric return via FLOW_TABLE-stored ingress ifindex (.3/.4/.5/.6 closed; local smoke + CI memory-smoke green incl. second-uplink round trip). REMAINING (deferred, out of the ratified MVP): asymmetric relay/egress-interface SELECTION (no bead yet -- file if v1 requires it); NODE_ALLOW multi-IP/multi-homed admission (beep-5ng). Bead stays OPEN for those. IPv6/dual-stack rides on top next (beep-7qm.2, lock-step).

title: test(loader): /0 + /32 boundary tests for vip_outside_pod_cidr + mask Ipv4Cidr.network (PR #3 review follow-ups)

title: docs(ebpf-lb): correct the LB-minted QUIC CID premise (CID is server/backend-chosen per RFC 9000 7.2, not LB-minted)
description: g3lag + aie31.11 research (2026-09-06) both found that ai/extended-context/ebpf-lb-dataplane.md (approx lines 99-111, 160) describes the routing Connection ID as minted by the LB. That premise is false for a non-terminating tc-bpf dataplane: per RFC 9000 section 7.2 the CID is server-chosen, and post-handshake CIDs travel in encrypted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames; the 1-RTT short header omits CID length (section 17.3.1). The only cooperation model is backend-generated routable CIDs the LB decodes (draft-ietf-quic-load-balancers), which requires backend opt-in and is Envoy-only today. Correct the doc so the CID claim reflects server/backend-chosen CIDs, and align the QUIC-exempt admission narrative. The false-premise correction stands regardless of the g3lag keying decision (a: 4-tuple pass-through vs b: QUIC-LB backend-cooperating); the surrounding narrative depends on which story the operator picks. APPLY task (Shape 6 durable doc) - do after the operator decides the keying story. See g3lag + aie31.11 findings docs on their worker branches.

title: net/servicelb: decide eBPF tc-bpf hook topology accounting for future TPROXY return-leg reuse -- single hook vs separate hooks, kernel perf and memory
description: L3 hook-topology design decision for the eBPF ServiceLB dataplane. A future L7 tier might reuse the existing symmetric-Geneve return path via TPROXY; account for that now when placing the tc-bpf hooks. If one hook point can safely and efficiently serve both ingress classification and a future TPROXY return leg, that is beneficial; if separate hooks are significantly cheaper on kernel memory or processing, that is fine too -- eBPF runs in-kernel, so this must be designed deliberately, not retrofitted. Kernel constraint to capture: node-local-originated traffic, for example a same-node proxy dialing the local node IP or VIP, is delivered by local routing and does not traverse the physical-NIC tc ingress qdisc, so a single hook on the physical uplink alone cannot serve the TPROXY return leg without an added local or loopback-aware hook. See the new Hook topology design note in ai/extended-context/ebpf-lb-dataplane.md. Stays on the aie31 L3 dataplane track; not a commitment to build L7 TPROXY.
notes:
Findings: ai/findings/2026-09-06-mayor-bguco-tc-bpf-hook-topology.md (branch worker/agent-ab570063b274c4d03, no PR). Recommendation: separate tc-bpf hooks sharing programs+maps, not one merged hook -- a same-node proxy dialing a local VIP goes via loopback and never crosses eth0 ingress, so facet 1 (classify proxy->VIP into Geneve) needs its own lo hook, while facet 2 (deliver Geneve-return to the local socket) reuses the existing geneve_ingress hook with only a terminal-action change; both memory and per-packet cost favor separate. Nothing built now; the one deferred data-model change is an origin flag in FWD_FLOW's value. Awaiting operator decision (see two open questions: proxy reuses VIP vs dials backends directly; hostNetwork/loopback vs Pod/veth placement).

title: design(servicelb): CID-based QUIC keying needs cluster-wide server_id-to-endpoint distribution, not just a per-node map
description: Operator raised 2026-09-07 on g3lag: the server-id-encoded CID (QUIC-LB draft) path the doc treats as a later opt-in has an un-spelled-out cross-node cost. Each node runs its own eBPF with its own map, so a per-node CID map cannot route a client that reconnects/migrates onto a DIFFERENT node. For server-id CID routing to work cluster-wide, EVERY node's eBPF needs (a) the shared CID-decode config (QUIC-LB encoding key/params, rotated in lockstep) and (b) a replicated server_id-to-backend-location table; a node lacking either cannot decode/route the CID. Operator's proposed mechanism (CONFIRMED correct + necessary): the cooperative L7 LB/backend allocates a persistent server_id per endpoint and publishes it via a CRD (or EndpointSlice/Pod annotation, or dedicated channel) that every node's userspace controller watches and programs into its eBPF map -- same distribution pattern as today's VIP/endpoint maps, keyed on server_id. UPSIDE worth recording: this scheme SOLVES cross-node reconnection/migration affinity that per-node conntrack FWD_FLOW pins fundamentally cannot (routing target travels in the CID, so any node decodes-and-routes statelessly; conntrack pins are node-local and break on cross-node reconnect). COST (reinforces g3lag's pass-through-now recommendation): threefold -- backend cooperation (only Envoy generates QUIC-LB CIDs today), shared+rotated decode secret across all nodes, and cluster-wide server_id-to-endpoint distribution. 4-tuple pass-through needs none of it, accepting only affinity-breaks-on-QUIC-migration. Coupling: same per-node convergence lag as 1dwwz drift, but smaller surface (per-endpoint-churn, not per-flow); tavxy delivery-node validation still bounds worst case to a drop. Action: fold into the g3lag findings doc's CID-based-later cost section; no code. Part of parked aie31 epic.
notes: RESEARCH RESULT (2026-09-07): Envoy does NOT publish a discoverable server_id-per-endpoint CRD. server_id is STATIC config (config.core.v3.DataSource: inline/file/env var; AWS EKS's NLB controller injects AWS_LBC_QUIC_SERVER_ID as a per-pod env var Envoy reads at startup). No xDS, no k8s resource surfaces the mapping. QUIC-LB draft explicitly puts parameter distribution OUT OF SCOPE (out-of-band). Envoy Gateway / Istio / Gateway API do not expose server_id. IMPLICATION: u7s must OWN the server_id distribution -- cannot observe an existing Envoy resource. Model: (1) u7s assigns the server_id space to nodes/endpoints, (2) publishes its OWN CRD/ConfigMap that its per-node eBPF watches for server_id->{backend}, (3) injects the IDs into Envoy (or the NLB controller does, on AWS). Net: CID-based keying requires u7s to BUILD+OWN an assignment+distribution+injection subsystem -- MORE machinery than 'observe Envoy', further reinforcing g3lag's pass-through-now recommendation. Refs: envoyproxy.io quic_lb.proto; quicwg.org load-balancers draft; aws-load-balancer-controller QUIC guide.

title: test-fidelity: conformance harness leaves #1525 podIP-allowlist dormant (node-ipam disabled in lima; prod SAFE via ipam+Flannel) — DEFERRED P3, revisit with eBPF/Flannel-uniform work
description: Surfaced live by mayor-ek41c (PR #1525). The whole elicb->ek41c chain built a CIDR-allowlist (podIP in node.spec.podCIDR) to close the arbitrary-external control-plane-SSRF class for non-hostNetwork pods. BUT this repo's conformance KCM (scripts/conformance/04-start-kcm.sh) runs with -node-ipam-controller DISABLED, so node.spec.podCIDR is NEVER populated (confirmed live: empty podCIDR on a Ready node; ek41c's strict impl 502'd every pod /proxy). ek41c ships a fallback: non-hostNetwork podIP is accepted blocklist-only when the node has no podCIDR (= the pre-ek41c k6m4a ceiling), with the allowlist auto-activating once a real per-node CIDR exists. So TODAY ek41c delivers only the hostNetwork loopback-floor + CRLF fixes; the non-hostNetwork arbitrary-external SSRF remains open (bounded by node-compromise, same residual). INVESTIGATE: (1) WHY is node-ipam-controller disabled -- deliberate (u7s networking model does not use per-node podCIDR allocation?) or incidental? (2) Does u7s's actual pod networking (CNI/CRI-O setup) assign pods from a per-node CIDR that node.spec.podCIDR could reflect, or is podIP allocation node-agnostic? If node-agnostic, the CIDR-allowlist approach is FUNDAMENTALLY inapplicable and blocklist-only (+hostNetwork floor) is the ceiling for this networking model -- a significant scoping conclusion. (3) If per-node CIDR IS viable, is enabling -node-ipam-controller (+ --cluster-cidr/--allocate-node-cidrs) safe here, and does it then activate ek41c's allowlist (re-run ek41c's kubectl SSRF repro with a populated podCIDR)? Outcome: either enable ipam (closes the class) or document that blocklist-only is the ceiling and re-scope the SSRF residual accordingly. No code change in this bead -- investigation + verdict. VM (stack-only) to test enabling ipam.
notes:
OPERATOR DOWNSCOPE (2026-09-02): don't investigate open-endedly — check whether node-ipam-controller has a dependency straight-up incompatible with u7s; if not, enable it and call it a day.

MAYOR PRE-DISPATCH FINDINGS (04-start-kcm.sh + lima-start.sh):
- ipam disabled at 04-start-kcm.sh:158 (--controllers '...,-node-ipam-controller,...'); no --cluster-cidr/--allocate-node-cidrs/--node-cidr-mask-size anywhere. Premise confirmed.
- u7s ALREADY uses per-node pod CIDRs, but assigned OUT-OF-BAND by lima-start.sh, NOT KCM: POD_SUBNET_OCTET (lima-start.sh:263-268) = suffix-1 (primary=0), pod subnet 10.85.<octet>.0/24, baked into CRI-O bridge CNI conflist (10-crio-bridge.conflist) + cni0 (line 303). Inter-node routes are static, no CNI/BGP (lima-start.sh:976).
- => Enabling KCM ipam adds a SECOND independent allocator. Compatibility hinges on whether KCM-assigned node.spec.podCIDR MATCHES the CNI's real 10.85.X.0/24. Single-node default topology: --cluster-cidr=10.85.0.0/16 --node-cidr-mask-size=24 => KCM assigns 10.85.0.0/24 to sole node = CNI 10.85.0.0/24 (likely MATCH). Multi-node: KCM registration-order vs lima-start.sh suffix-order can DRIFT.
- RISK: a MISMATCHED podCIDR is strictly worse than status quo — #1525's allowlist activates and REJECTS legit pods. Worker MUST verify the match live before shipping; ship only if it matches, else report incompatibility + revert + file follow-on for the deeper align-allocators fix.
- Also verify KCM (controller-manager SA, not a node) writing spec.podCIDR is NOT blocked by mayor-elicb's NodeRestriction-equivalent admission (#1518).

SEQUENCING: elmno's allowlist-activation check needs #1525's proxy code, not yet on main. Dispatch elmno off FRESH main AFTER #1525 merges.
OPERATOR REFRAMING (2026-09-02) — corrects my earlier 'two competing allocators / drift risk' framing: lima-start.sh's per-node CIDR assignment is a STAND-IN for the disabled ipam controller, NOT a competing allocator. Design intent: enable node-ipam-controller => KCM becomes the SINGLE source of truth for node.spec.podCIDR; lima-start.sh should no longer COMPUTE the subnet. Drift concern dissolves (one allocator).

IMPLEMENTATION NUANCE (makes this a moderate refactor, not a one-liner): CRI-O's stock bridge CNI reads a STATIC conflist (/etc/cni/net.d/10-crio-bridge.conflist) and does NOT natively consume node.spec.podCIDR. So 'script no longer needs to do it' concretely = lima-start.sh stops computing POD_SUBNET from node suffix (lima-start.sh:263-268) and instead READS KCM's assigned node.spec.podCIDR and writes THAT into the conflist. Two knock-ons: (1) BOOTSTRAP ORDERING — today the subnet is set at node bring-up; with ipam it must WAIT for KCM to assign podCIDR before pods can schedule; (2) INTER-NODE STATIC ROUTES (lima-start.sh:976,1006-1007, keyed off the suffix-computed POD_SUBNET) must switch to KCM's podCIDR.

REVISED elmno scope (still behind #1525/npjfm):
1. Enable node-ipam-controller in 04-start-kcm.sh (remove from --controllers disable list :158; add --allocate-node-cidrs=true --cluster-cidr=10.85.0.0/16 --node-cidr-mask-size=24 so KCM's scheme matches the existing 10.85.<octet>.0/24 addressing).
2. Rework lima-start.sh: source the CNI conflist subnet + inter-node routes from KCM's node.spec.podCIDR instead of suffix arithmetic; handle wait-for-podCIDR ordering.
3. Verify KCM (controller-manager SA) writing spec.podCIDR is NOT blocked by mayor-elicb's NodeRestriction admission (#1518).
4. Verify end-to-end live (VM): node gets podCIDR from KCM -> CNI uses it -> real pods get IPs within it -> #1525/npjfm allowlist ACTIVATES and legit non-hostNetwork pod proxy still works (re-run ek41c SSRF repro with a populated podCIDR). Multi-node optional but ideal.
OPERATOR PRIORITY (2026-09-02): test-setup SIMPLICITY over architectural purity. If KCM-authoritative is complicated (KCM comes online AFTER the CIDR is assumed configured), prefer a simpler option.

DECISION -> go SIMPLE (supersedes the earlier 'KCM-authoritative, rework lima-start.sh' scope in the prior note):
- Enable node-ipam-controller in 04-start-kcm.sh (remove from --controllers disable list :158; add --allocate-node-cidrs=true --cluster-cidr=10.85.0.0/16 --node-cidr-mask-size=24 so KCM's allocation MATCHES lima-start.sh's existing 10.85.<octet>.0/24 scheme).
- LEAVE lima-start.sh's CNI subnet computation UNCHANGED (lima-start.sh:263-268). It keeps setting the CNI subnet at node bring-up as today -> pods schedule immediately, NO wait-for-podCIDR, NO bootstrap reorder, NO inter-node-route rework. KCM merely populates the node.spec.podCIDR FIELD alongside; #1525/npjfm allowlist falls back to blocklist-only until the field appears, then activates.
- Single-node (default conformance topology): KCM's podCIDR = lima-start.sh's CNI subnet = 10.85.0.0/24 by construction -> allowlist activates, nothing to reconcile.
- CAVEAT (document, don't fix unless required): multi-node runs can DRIFT (KCM registration-order vs lima-start.sh suffix-order); a mismatched podCIDR would make the allowlist reject legit cross-node pods. Only if multi-node conformance-under-allowlist becomes a hard requirement do we revisit the complex KCM-authoritative design (lima-start.sh reads podCIDR).

WORKER VERIFY LIVE (VM, single-node): (1) KCM (controller-manager SA) writing spec.podCIDR is NOT blocked by mayor-elicb NodeRestriction (#1518); (2) node gets podCIDR 10.85.0.0/24 matching the CNI subnet; (3) #1525/npjfm allowlist ACTIVATES and legit non-hostNetwork pod proxy still works (re-run ek41c SSRF repro with populated podCIDR); (4) conformance smoke still green. Still queued behind #1525/npjfm merge.

The dormancy is CONFORMANCE-HARNESS-ONLY: lima-start.sh (963) uses CRI-O's stock static bridge CNI 'no CNI swap needed' for test speed, and 04-start-kcm.sh:158 disables node-ipam-controller, then lima-start.sh computes 10.85.<octet>.0/24 out-of-band. The earlier 'simple path' (align cluster-cidr, keep lima-start.sh computing) and 'deterministic write' are BOTH backwards from prod (harness stays an independent allocator) — reject. Running worker a8c0431f paused; simple-path PR NOT to be opened. Operator deciding: do the consume-model fix now vs defer (prod already safe).
LIVE EVIDENCE from worker a8c0431f (2026-09-02, VM lima-node-4, since cleaned up — no PR, elmno left open):

title: servicelb-ebpf: backend src-port remap re-derives every packet -> LRU eviction reassigns port mid-connection
description: From #1567 pa0ze round-3 critical review (MED, review 5115377623, confirmed by execution). resolve_backend_src_port (crates/servicelb/servicelb-common/src/lib.rs ~165) re-derives the synthetic backend src-port from the same deterministic seed on EVERY packet with no persisted decision. If an LRU eviction removes an UNRELATED occupant at an earlier probe index between two packets of the same flow, the flow re-probes, finds that earlier slot now free, and commits a DIFFERENT port mid-connection -> reverse-path breakage. Only manifests under map-full LRU eviction pressure (conntrack maps are LRU_HASH). Robust fix: persist the flow's chosen synthetic port in its FWD_FLOW state and read it back on subsequent packets instead of re-deriving (approach (a) from the round-3 brief) -- idempotent by construction, no re-probe. Test under eviction: commit port_X, free an earlier-probe-index occupant, assert the next packet still resolves to port_X. RELATED: mayor-lrbvo (Phase-4 real-fleet churn/eviction + RSS measurement) is the natural home to validate this under real pressure; the PR already defers general churn/eviction there. This is a narrower, specific instance of that deferral, tracked so it is not lost.
notes: BLOCKED on aie31.17 (operator decision 2026-09-08). Fix-round proved node-locality makes clean persistence impossible without the unified-flow-table redesign: backend_src_port is decided+re-read on the BACKEND node (try_geneve_decap_forward), FWD_MAIN/FWD_PENDING are ingress-node-only, BPF maps are per-node. Round-1 (#1628, closed unmerged) added a 2nd REV_FLOW key under (VIP,client) front_key -> finding-2 collision risk (VIP/pod-CIDR NOT disjoint for hostNetwork Pods, per aie31.17) + doubled occupancy. Resolve as part of / after aie31.17's explicit-tag unified table.

title: servicelb-ebpf: uplink parse hard-codes Ethernet L2 (ETH_HLEN=14) -- silently no-ops on L3-only uplinks (WireGuard/overlay)
description: WireGuard-over-Lima spike (2026-09-04, lrbvo) found: uplink_ingress/uplink_egress_return in crates/servicelb/servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs hard-code ETH_HLEN=14 and read the EtherType at ctx.load::<u16>(12), then index the IPv4 header at ETH_HLEN-relative offsets. A WireGuard (or any L3-only/tun) uplink has NO 14-byte Ethernet header, so the EtherType load reads into the middle of the real IP header, never matches 0x0800, and the program falls through to TC_ACT_OK on every packet -- the dataplane SILENTLY no-ops on an L3 uplink (no crash). Blocks Phase-4 tier-1 (Lima/VPS over WireGuard) and any overlay/L3 uplink. FIX: make the header-skip conditional (0 for L3-only, 14 for Ethernet) -- e.g. a load-time flag from the loader (it knows the iface type) or runtime detection. The tc-bpf ATTACH to an L3/no-L2 wg iface ALREADY WORKS (spike proved via bpftool); this is purely the parse-offset assumption. SHARED SURFACE with pa0ze/#1567 (servicelb-ebpf) -- dispatch AFTER #1567 merges. Verify via the smoke harness (attach + round-trip) on a wg uplink.
